☆ $C^{1,α}$ Regularity of $W^{2,2}$ $Q$-Valued Maps with Small Laplacian
Mattia Luchese
We establish a regularity criterion for $Q$-valued maps $u\in W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω,\mathcal A_Q(\mathbb R^k))$, where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $|Δu|\leqδ_*|D^2u|$ almost everywhere, with $δ_*=δ_*(n,k,Q)>0$ sufficiently small, then $u\in C^{1,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $α=α(n,k,Q)>0$, with quantitative estimates. The result holds for arbitrary $n\geq2$, $k\geq1$, and $Q\geq1$. The proof establishes uniform energy decay using a rigidity principle for positive-semidefinite matrix-valued measures with an aperture bound and approximately atomic divergence, extending the target-stress argument for the homogeneity gap in \cite{Luc26}. The argument relies only on first variation identities. As consequences, we obtain $C^{1,α}$ regularity for Dirichlet-stationary $W^{2,2}$ maps and for locally Lipschitz $W^{2,2}$ maps whose graph varifolds are stationary and have sufficiently small slope. Combining the latter result with Bellettini's Lipschitz sheeting theorem \cite{Bel25}, we establish $C^{1,α}$ sheeting in the multiple-valued sense for two-sided stable minimal immersions whose singular set has vanishing $2$-capacity relative to the immersion, under suitable flatness and mass bounds. Our results allow us to reduce the proof of compactness within this class, under locally uniform mass bounds, to the conjecture that branch sets of stationary $C^{1,α}$ multiple-valued graphs in codimension one have vanishing $2$-capacity.
☆ A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
Xuwen Chen, Justin Holmer, Shunlin Shen
We consider the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a bounded forward-global solution which starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The core has two limits in distinct similarity orbits. A single energy-space norm identity identifies the radiation and reduces every competing fixed list to one profile; the two limits then give a contradiction. The construction uses summable radiation packets whose quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. We control the nonlinear error uniformly over these intervals and select the endpoints by a compact fixed-point map. A computer-assisted certificate validates the stationary state and its complete odd energy kernel.

☆ Nonrigidity of smooth tight surfaces
Mohammad Ghomi, Hongda Qiu, Matteo Raffaelli, Yuetong Zhang
We construct smooth isometric embeddings of closed surfaces of positive genus in Euclidean 3-space which are tight, i.e., have minimal total positive curvature, but are not congruent. These embeddings agree outside a compact subset of the region of negative curvature, and enclose different volumes. Thus the rigidity theorem of Alexandrov for analytic tight surfaces does not hold in the smooth category, which settles problems of Nirenberg and Banchoff-Kuhnel.

☆ Stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions seven and eight
Serena Dipierro, Joaquim Serra, Raphael Tsiamis, Enrico Valdinoci
We establish optimal sheet separation estimates for stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions up to seven, using an iteration argument in the nonlocal approximation theory of Chan-Dipierro-Serra-Valdinoci. These estimates imply that every stable $s$-minimal hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a hyperplane when $s$ is close to $1$. More generally, every finite Morse index $s$-minimal set in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a half-space. We also establish a compactness theorem for stable $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$. We prove uniform curvature and area estimates for their links and show that, as $s \uparrow 1$, they subconverge graphically in $C^{2,α}$, either with multiplicity one to a classical stable minimal cone, or with multiplicity two to a hyperplane. The stability of Lawson and axisymmetric $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$ shows that these results are optimal.
☆ Radiation and persistent shape dynamics for the five-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear wave equation
Xuwen Chen, Justin Holmer, Shunlin Shen
We consider the nonradial five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a forward-global solution which remains arbitrarily close to a nondegenerate sign-changing stationary state in the energy space and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The stationary profile moves in a compact conformal family, but its limit set contains a continuum of classes modulo translations, dilations and rotations. Consequently, the solution admits no soliton resolution using a fixed finite collection of stationary profiles and fixed Lorentz velocities, with pairwise orthogonal spatial parameters. That is, we disprove the fixed-profile soliton resolution conjecture for the five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. The construction uses a sequence of incoming waves with summable energies. Their quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. The main estimates control the zero eigenvalue of the linearized operator and the nonlinear error uniformly over the entire sequence. The stationary input uses a computer-assisted spectral bound for a symmetric single-node state.

☆ Qualitative properties of solutions to anisotropic parabolic equations: Part III- Hölder continuity
Simone Ciani, Eurica Henriques, Maria O. Savchenko, Igor I. Skrypnik
In this work, we study the local Hölder continuity of non-negative solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear anisotropic partial differential equations, with prototype \[ u_t-\sum_{i=1}^N D_i\Big(|D_i u^{m_i}|^{p_i-2}D_i u^{m_i}\Big)=0, \quad m_i>0,\quad p_i>1,\quad i=1,\ldots,N. \] The main result shows that, when the exponents describing the diffusion in different spatial directions are sufficiently close to one another, the solutions enjoy local Hölder continuity. A key feature of the analysis is the distinction between two diffusion regimes: the degenerate and the singular cases; the local regularity results are established in both regimes, under suitable conditions on the exponents.
☆ Higher integrability for parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with gradient-dependent sources
Yan Li, Zhiwen Zhao
This paper aims to establish higher gradient integrability away from the initial time for solutions to parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with general gradient-dependent lower-order terms throughout the singular and degenerate regimes. For this purpose, we develop an elliptic reconstruction argument based on an $L^2$-valued temporal Hölder estimate, thereby transferring the problem to elliptic estimates and quantitative control of the reconstruction error. In particular, our approach yields an explicit higher-integrability exponent. We further construct counterexamples illustrating that bounded continuous initial data alone are insufficient to ensure higher gradient integrability up to the initial time. Finally, we provide counterexamples demonstrating that gradient-dependent lower-order terms can prevent temporal Lipschitz regularity.
☆ Convergence rates for smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) with nonlinear pressure
Piotr Gwiazda, Jakub Skrzeczkowski, Jakub Woźnicki
We establish quantitative convergence results for the smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method approximating the compressible Euler equations with nonlinear pressure laws $ρ^γ$, $γ\geq 2$. Our approach is based on a nonlocal approximation of the pressure force that preserves the energy structure of the original system, including an exact energy balance. Using the relative entropy method, we prove convergence towards smooth solutions of the compressible Euler equations as the nonlocality parameter $\varepsilon\to0$, with algebraic convergence rates and an explicit algebraic relationship between $\varepsilon$ and the number of particles $N$. In particular, we obtain quantitative convergence rates for the density in the Wasserstein distance and negative Sobolev norms, and for the momentum in the flat metric. A key feature of our analysis is that it applies to measure-valued densities in the nonlocal system, providing a unified framework for both continuum and particle solutions. Our results extend the existing rigorous convergence theory for SPH beyond quadratic pressure ($γ=2$) to general nonlinear pressure laws with $γ\geq 2$ on the periodic domain.

☆ Discrete unique continuation for Schrödinger equations
Torunn S. Jensen, Didier Pilod, João P. G. Ramos
We study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional Schrödinger equations. We prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^α$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^β$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a Schrödinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of Gevrey class $σ\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,σ\}\big(α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, provided that $α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)<1$. Unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. We first show that, whenever $α+β<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the Schwartz class at all times. We then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $Γ=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from Fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the Morgan-type uncertainty principle of Escauriaza, Kenig, Ponce and Vega.

☆ On a PDE-ODE-ODE model for meniscus tissue regeneration with space-dependent, possibly degenerate diffusion tensor
Nishith Mohan, Ahmad Hussein, Bernd Simeon, Christina Surulescu
We investigate a tissue regeneration model that describes the coupled dynamics of human mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), chondrocytes, and newly formed extracellular matrix (ECM). The system features motility terms only for the mesenchymal stem cells, more precisely myopic diffusion and haptotaxis towards increasing ECM; all of those terms involve a space-dependent, possibly degenerating tensor. The chondrocytes are obtained from MSCs by differentiation and provide positive feedback to MSCs via dedifferentiation. The considered macroscopic model was obtained by upscaling from a formulation within the kinetic theory of active particles. Under appropriate assumptions we prove global existence of classical solutions in 2D and 3D in the case of a nondegenerating tensor and global existence of weak solutions in 2D when the diffusion tensor is allowed to degenerate. Numerical simulations are performed in 2D in order to illustrate the solution behavior.

☆ Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation
Lingda Xu
We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. ☆ Off-diagonal decay of capacitance matrices via Brownian motion

☆ Cavity collapse and vorticity gradient blow-up in free-boundary Euler flow
Tao Luo, Siqi Yang
We construct smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations with surface tension whose vorticity remains bounded while its full spatial gradient blows up in finite time. The solutions are axisymmetric without swirl and occupy bounded domains in which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at time $T$, while the outer free surface converges smoothly. The vorticity $ω$ can be chosen arbitrarily small in $L^\infty$, uniformly up to collapse, and satisfies $\|\nablaω(t)\|_{L^\infty}\asymp (T-t)^{-1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{1/4}$ as $t\uparrow T$. A nonconstant material trace of the relative vorticity on the shrinking surface determines direction-dependent limits of the terminal vorticity, which therefore has no continuous extension across the collapse circle. The kinetic energy measure converges to the sum of a uniform line measure on this circle and a nonzero bulk part carried by a bounded rotational field. The construction couples vorticity transport to the boundary dynamics through weighted estimates in the collapsing collar and a cancellation in the normal acceleration.

☆ On the quasi-static growth of cavities in incompressible elastomers
Marco Bresciani, Giuliano Lazzaroni
For a variational model of incompressible elastomers exhibiting cavitation, we establish the existence of irreversible quasi-static evolutions driven by time-dependent boundary conditions. The proof employs the multiplicative splitting introduced by Francfort and Mielke (2006) to reduce the problem to time-independent boundary conditions and then invokes abstract results on the existence of energetic solutions to rate-independent systems. Specifically, the construction of mutual recovery sequences requires particular attention to accommodate the incompressibility constraint: to this end we employ the method by Moser (1965) to exhibit incompressible diffeomorphisms interpolating between localized translations and the identity.

We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. Luo Yue
We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $ν^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $ν$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-rν^{\frac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-νt}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim ν^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $ν$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$.

We provide a method to construct a real-analytic ideal MHD equilibrium $(B,p)$ in a solid toroidal domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}$, with $B$ tangential to the boundary $\partialΩ$. A compatible adjoint identity yields a reconstruction method with a conditional stability estimate on any fixed finite-dimensional space of smooth displacements. ☆ Sharp low-dimensional Constants in the second-order hydrogen Heisenberg uncertainty principle via Jacobi chains

This paper addresses a two-phase fluid system on the periodic domain $\mathbb{T}^3$, consisting of the pressureless Euler equations and the incompressible non-Newtonian equations coupled through a drag force. We prove the global-in-time existence of strong solutions to this system for a certain class of stress tensors in the non-Newtonian fluid. Our proof combines a priori large-time behavior estimates for classical solutions with a bootstrapping argument on the $L^2$-Sobolev norms, which effectively handles the difficulties caused by the lack of dissipation in the density of the Euler equation.
☆ Maximum Principles and Principal Eigenvalue for Coupled Local/Nonlocal Models
Willian Cintra, Jônatas Peralta, Julio D. Rossi, Antonio Suárez
In this paper, we analyze the validity of the maximum principle and the existence of a principal eigenvalue for a problem involving two regions, in one of them the main operator is the classical Laplacian (a local operator) while in the other region the operator is a nonlocal one (these regions are coupled via a transmission term that is also nonlocal). The main difficulty here comes from the lack of compactness of the nonlocal part that occurs since we are considering non-singular kernels.
♻ ☆ Parabolic stochastic quantisation of the fractional $Φ^4_3$ model in the full subcritical regime
Paweł Duch, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Paolo Rinaldi
We present a construction of the measure of the fractional $Φ^4$ Euclidean quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^3$ in the full subcritical regime via parabolic stochastic quantisation. Our approach is based on a truncated flow equation for the effective description of the model at sufficiently small scales and on coercive estimates for the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation describing the interacting field. The constructed measure is translation invariant, reflection positive, and has quartic exponential tails.
comment: 136 pages, published version
♻ ☆ Averaging Dynamics and Wong-Zakai approximations for a Fast-Slow Navier-Stokes System Driven by fractional Brownian Motion
Eliseo Luongo, Francesco Triggiano
We study a Fast-Slow system of coupled two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations in which the fast component is perturbed by an additive fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $\H>\frac{1}{3}$. Using rough path theory, we establish subsequential convergence in law of the slow component, with limiting dynamics depending on the Hurst parameter and the noise scaling. For $\H<\frac12$, an averaging regime yields a deterministic Navier-Stokes equation with an additional Itô-Stokes drift. Under a stronger noise scaling, corresponding to a Wong-Zakai approximation, and a centering condition on the quadratic fast dynamics, we obtain a Navier-Stokes equation driven by fractional transport noise. For $\H>\frac12$, the transport-noise limit holds in the Wong-Zakai regime without this centering condition, with integration understood in the Young sense.
comment: This version includes an improved Wong-Zakai result for the case H<1/2. Comments are welcome
♻ ☆ Higher integrability for parabolic double phase equations with an improved gap bound
Abhrojyoti Sen, Jarkko Siltakoski
We prove a local higher integrability result for the gradient of \textit{a priori} Hölder continuous weak solutions to the parabolic double phase equation \[ \partial_t u - \operatorname{div} \left(|Du|^{p-2}Du + a(z)|Du|^{q-2}Du\right) = 0 \qquad \text{in } Ω_T. \] We work under a relaxed gap condition on the exponents $p$ and $q$. The coefficient $a$ is assumed to belong to the class $\mathcal{Z}^κ(Ω_T)$ for some $κ\in (0,\infty)$. The functions in this class satisfy a one-sided pointwise bound that controls how fast $a$ can grow away from its zero set, and the class contains the Hölder continuous functions. We also impose a \emph{mild almost increasing} condition on $a$, which motivates the introduction of a new mollification, which we call the \emph{slanted Steklov average}. For $u \in C^{0,γ,γ/q}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω_T)$ with $γ\in [0,1)$, our main result holds under the gap bound \begin{equation}\tag{G}\label{eq:G} 2 \le p \le q, \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, (q-p)(q-2γ)\leq qκ\end{equation} The new gap condition \eqref{eq:G} is purely parabolic in nature and is stricter than the optimal gap relation associated with the Lavrentiev phenomenon for the elliptic double phase functional.
comment: 42 pages, to appear in Advances in Calculus of Variations
♻ ☆ Gradient estimates and Liouville properties for the drifted Laplacian
Salvatore Lincastri
In this paper, we discuss the validity of Liouville-type theorems involving the drifted Laplacian on complete, non-compact Riemannian manifolds endowed with a smooth vector field $X$. In particular, we prove new Liouville properties both for positive $X$-harmonic functions and for non-negative $X$-subharmonic functions which are in an $L^{p}$-space, $p\in(1,+\infty)$, with respect to any invariant measure for the operator. The main tool for the analysis is a local gradient estimate for positive solutions to the semilinear equation $Δ_{X}u=F(u)$, which is valid if $F$ satisfies certain structural conditions and the Bakry-Émery-Ricci curvature associated to $X$ is bounded below. On the one hand, this estimate is used in a novel way to deduce the Liouville property for positive solutions and, on the other hand, it is used to construct cut-off functions for the $X$-Laplacian that yields the $L^{p}$-Liouville results.
comment: 30 pages. Added Section 5, concerning X-Laplacian cut-off functions and $L^p$-Liouville properties with respect to invariant measures. Substantial revisions to the Introduction. All comments are welcome!
♻ ☆ Improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri Inequalities under Constraints: Sharpness and Quantitative Remainders
Yuxuan Zhou, Wenming Zou
In this paper, we study improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities on the sphere under moment constraints, with particular emphasis on sharp leading constants and quantitative remainder terms. For the Sobolev inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequality of Hang and Wang [30] (Int. Math. Res. Not., 2022) to a sharp one at $p=2$ under vanishing moment constraints of orders $m=1,2,3$. We also prove a general failure principle: if the unconstrained sharp Sobolev inequality fails, then the corresponding sharp improved inequality under moment constraints fails as well. For the Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequalities of Chang and Hang [10] and Hang [29] (Comm. Pure Appl. Math., 2022) to a sharp improved inequality at the critical order $s=\frac{n}{2}$ under arbitrary finite-order moment constraints. We further investigate the best remainder constant. In contrast with the two-dimensional first-moment case of Gui and Moradifam [28] (Invent. Math., 2018), where the best remainder vanishes, we show that it is positive in several higher-dimensional regimes. We also obtain quantitative remainder estimates for general almost sharp improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities, which in turn yield sharp inequalities at different scales. We further extend recent second-moment refinements to higher dimensions and higher orders. Finally, we obtain analogous results on sharpness, non-sharpness, and quantitative remainder estimates for improved Sobolev-type inequalities under symmetry constraints on general smooth closed manifolds.
comment: Originally submitted to a journal on September 17, 2026. v2: Added a note on related independent works and updated the references. Main results unchanged
♻ ☆ Sharp asymptotic stability of the IPM equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via isopycnal coordinates
Roberta Bianchini, Timothée Crin-Barat, Ling-Yun Shou, Shan Wang
We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data. The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.
♻ ☆ Global regularity and sharp decay rates for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces
Chen Liang, Zhaonan Luo, Zhaoyang Yin
In this paper, we study the global regularity for the one-dimensional hypo-viscous compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the critical Besov spaces, where the initial data are close to the constant equilibrium state. We introduce an effective velocity, constructed as a combination of the density and the velocity, which is used to capture the high-frequency behavior of $a$. By performing elaborate high-frequency and low-frequency estimates together with a bootstrap argument, we obtain global existence for $\frac{1}{2}\leβ<1$. In particular, when $β=\frac{1}{2}$, we also prove the system is well-posed in critical space. Furthermore, under an additional low-frequency assumption, we establish the optimal time decay rates.
♻ ☆ The $m$-Laplace equation with a gradient term I: Liouville theorem in the second subcritical case
Tian Wu, Jin Yan, Hua Zhu
Let $10$, and $p\in\mathbb R$. We study positive $C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ weak solutions of \[-Δ_m u=u^p|Du|^q\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^n.\] If $0
♻ ☆ The stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb{R}^{7}$
Han Hong, Haizhong Li, Gaoming Wang
We give a Green-function proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb R^7$ for smooth, connected, complete, two-sided stable minimal hypersurfaces, thus resolving the last case of the stable Bernstein problem.
comment: 47 pages. Improved exposition and simplified proofs. All comments are welcome
♻ ☆ Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
Lorenzo Luciano Morelato, Andrea Poggio
This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragičević for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schrödinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
comment: In v2 we have slightly modified the presentation of our results and added the example of magnetic Schrödinger operators; 65 pages
♻ ☆ Pitt Inequalities and Logarithmic-type Uncertainty Principles for Metaplectic Operators
Gianluca Giacchi, Itamar Oliveira, Amy Tierney
In this work, we provide a complete characterisation of Pitt's inequality for metaplectic operators. The symplectic geometry underlying a metaplectic operator distinguishes effective directions, along which its action is Fourier-type, from singular directions, along which concentration is preserved. For this reason, we adopt two complementary perspectives, thereby obtaining both an isotropic Pitt's inequality, emulating the classical theorem of Pitt, and an anisotropic inequality that adapts to the geometric features of the metaplectic group. As a by-product, we obtain Pitt's inequality for Fourier transforms along subspaces of $\rd$ and new quantitative time-dependent boundedness results for metaplectic operators on homogeneous Sobolev spaces, with applications to Schrödinger evolutions generated by quadratic Hamiltonians. Additionally, we derive logarithmic and entropic uncertainty principles for the metaplectic group. We show that the classical entropic uncertainty principle fails when both the effective and singular directions are present. In this case, a generally unbounded corrective entropy term accounts for the concentration-preserving directions and restores a meaningful lower bound. For quadratic Schrödinger evolutions, this correction follows the time-dependent geometry of the nondispersive directions and adjusts the uncertainty estimate accordingly.
comment: Journal feedback was implemented
♻ ☆ Optimizing the ground state energy of the three-dimensional magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field
Matthias Baur
This paper concerns the shape optimization problem of minimizing the ground state energy of the magnetic Dirichlet Laplacian with constant magnetic field among three-dimensional domains of fixed volume. In contrast to the two-dimensional case, a generalized "magnetic" Faber-Krahn inequality does not hold and minimizers cannot be balls when the magnetic field is turned on. An analysis of the problem among cylindrical domains reveals geometric constraints for general minimizers. In particular, minimizers must elongate with a certain rate along the direction of the magnetic field as the field strength increases. In addition to the theoretical analysis, we present numerical minimizers which confirm this prediction and give rise to further conjectures.
comment: 24 pages, 4 figures; updated to the final published version
♻ ☆ A convex integration scheme for the continuity equation past the Sobolev embedding threshold
Maria Colombo, Roberto Colombo, Anuj Kumar
We introduce a convex integration scheme for the continuity equation in the context of the Di Perna-Lions theory that allows to build incompressible vector fields in $C_{t}W^{1,p}_x$ and nonunique solutions in $C_{t} L^{q}_x$ for any $p,q$ with $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} > 1 + \frac{1}{d}- δ$ for some $δ>0$. This improves the previous bound, corresponding to $δ=0$, or equivalently $q' > p^*$, obtained with convex integration so far, and critical for those schemes in view of the Sobolev embedding that guarantees that solutions are distributional in the opposite range.
comment: 24 pages
♻ ☆ On a fractional Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman-type monotonicity formula
Fausto Ferrari, Davide Giovagnoli, Enzo Maria Merlino
In this paper, by exploiting mean value properties of $s$-harmonic functions, we introduce some monotonicity formulas in the nonlocal setting. Our approach is purely nonlocal and does not rely on the extension technique. As a byproduct we also establish interior nonlocal gradient estimates and a nonlocal analogue of the Bochner identity.
♻ ☆ Spectral gaps and uniqueness in the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem
Yao Wan
We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.
comment: Updated version. 21 pages. All comments are welcome
♻ ☆ Boundary value problems for 0-elliptic operators
Marco Usula
Let $X$ be a manifold with boundary, and let $L$ be a 0-elliptic operator on X which is semi-Fredholm essentially surjective with infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples include Hodge Laplacians and Dirac operators on conformally compact manifolds. We construct left and right parametrices for L when supplemented with appropriate elliptic boundary conditions. The construction relies on a new calculus of pseudodifferential operators on functions over both $X$ and $\partial X$, which we call the "symbolic 0-calculus". This new calculus supplements the ordinary 0-calculus of Mazzeo--Melrose, enabling it to handle boundary value problems. In the original 0-calculus, operators are characterized as polyhomogeneous right densities on a blow-up of $X^2$. By contrast, operators in the symbolic 0-calculus are characterized (locally near each point of the boundary of the diagonal) as quantizations of polyhomogeneous symbols on appropriate blown-up model spaces.
comment: 153 pages, 8 figures. Version published by Ars Inveniendi Analytica. Major changes from v1: 1. Addition of a "guiding example" (§2.6, §3.5, §6.5 §7.3) illustrating the theory. 2. Addition of a section (§7) with a new regularity theorem for solutions of 0-elliptic equations
♻ ☆ A Spacetime-Diffeomorphic Approach to Magnetohydrodynamics around Black Holes: Dilation Covariance, Linearization,and the No-Hair Limit
Yuanya Li
The ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system that governs a conducting plasma---the Maxwell equations together with the conservation laws of mass, momentum and energy---is the same local balance structure that describes hot accretion flows around black holes. We introduce a uniform four-dimensional spacetime dilation \[ Φ_L:\;(t',x',y',z')\mapsto (t,x,y,z)=(Lt',Lx',Ly',Lz'),\qquad L>1, \] and show that it is a smooth, orientation-preserving $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of flat spacetime. Pulling the MHD conservation laws back through $Φ_L$, we prove that the closed ideal-MHD system is form-invariant (covariant), with the current density rescaling as $\bm j=\bm j'/L$, the magnetic diffusivity as $η'=η/L$, and external sources rescaled by $L$. The transformation realises three physically distinct effects on the perturbed flow: a \emph{linearization} to the tangent-space (linearised MHD) system, a \emph{movie slow-motion} dilation of dissipative and dynamical timescales, and an \emph{electron-microscope} magnification of small-scale structure. Taking the formal limit $L\to\infty$ localises the dynamics on a neighbourhood of a horizon: resistivity vanishes, the asymptotic time derivative freezes, and all transient multipolar structure of the infalling plasma redshifts away. The remaining stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat electrovacuum is uniquely the Kerr--Newman geometry, so that the exterior of the compact object is characterised only by its mass $M$, angular momentum $J$ and charge $Q$. The result provides a local, conservation-law-based perspective on the black hole no-hair theorem that is complementary to the classical Israel--Carter-- Robinson theorems and to contemporary gravitational-wave and Event Horizon Telescope tests.
♻ ☆ Sufficient conditions for multiplicity and uniqueness of positive solutions of the Hénon equation
Geyang Du
We establish explicit sufficient conditions for multiplicity of positive solutions of the Hénon equation in the unit ball and for uniqueness in one dimension. In the Sobolev-subcritical range, a spherical harmonic function argument shows that the radial solution has Morse index greater than one and therefore differs from a ground state. In even dimensions, a degree-four perturbation in a symmetry and monotonicity cone yields a sufficient condition for nonradiality in the supercritical range. The one-dimensional uniqueness criterion follows from a comparison of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues and a concavity estimate.
comment: 12 pages, 1 figure
♻ ☆ Global existence, blow-up behavior and numerical simulations for a class of chemotaxis-driven fish-mussel systems
Gnanasekaran Shanmugasundaram, Jitraj Saha
In this work, we investigate a chemotaxis-driven fish--mussel ecosystem model described by a coupled system of partial differential equations subject to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. Under suitable assumptions on the system parameters and initial data, we establish the global existence of classical solutions by employing semigroup methods together with a priori estimates. We also examine the possible blow-up behavior of solutions in a three-dimensional domain. To support the theoretical analysis, a finite element method is developed for the numerical approximation of the system, and convergence studies based on mesh refinement are carried out to verify the accuracy and stability of the proposed numerical scheme. Furthermore, numerical simulations illustrating the blow-up behavior of solutions in the computational domain are presented.
♻ ☆ Dissipative solutions for 2D Onsager's conjecture
Lili Du, Xinliang Li, Weikui Ye
In 1949, L. Onsager conjectured that weak solutions of the Euler equations in $C_{t,x}^γ$ are energy conservative when $γ>\frac{1}{3}$, whereas nonconservative solutions exist when $γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Constantin, E and Titi [13] proved the conservation part, while Isett [26] constructed nontrivial $C^γ_{t,x}$ weak solutions with compact support in time in three dimensions for each $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Building on this breakthrough work, Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi Jr. and Vicol [7] obtained strictly dissipative solutions below the Onsager threshold. In two dimensions, Giri and Radu [23] first constructed a nontrivial weak solution in $C^{\frac{1}{3}-}(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ and left an open problem whether it would be possible to construct dissipative solutions (controllable energy) below $\frac{1}{3}$ threshold. In this paper, we reslove this question and thereby obtain infinitely many strictly dissipative weak solutions in $C^γ(\mathbb T^2\times[0,T])$ for every $0<γ<\frac{1}{3}$. Moreover, we prove that the associated wild initial data are dense in the divergence-free subspace of $C^{γ'}(\mathbb{T}^2)$ for any $0<γ' <\frac{1}{3}$. The key new ingredient is a family of staircase traveling waves, which we combine with a Picard iteration coupled to the Newton--Nash scheme to control both the Reynolds stress and the kinetic energy. The construction also applies in every dimension $d\geq2$.
♻ ☆ Nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian: Existence, non-existence and uniqueness results
Rakesh Arora, Jacques Giacomoni, Arshi Vaishnavi
In this work, we study the existence, non-existence, and uniqueness results for nonlocal elliptic equations involving logarithmic Laplacian, and subcritical, critical, and supercritical logarithmic nonlinearities. The Poho\u zaev's identity and Díaz-Saa type inequality are proved, which are of independent interest and can be applied to a larger class of problems. Depending upon the growth of nonlinearities and regularity of the weight function, we study the small-order asymptotic of nonlocal weighted elliptic equations involving the fractional Laplacian of order $2s.$ We show that the least energy solutions of a weighted nonlocal problem with superlinear or sublinear growth converge to a nontrivial nonnegative least-energy solution of Brézis-Nirenberg type and logistic-type limiting problem respectively involving the logarithmic Laplacian.
comment: Due to a mistake in the proof of Pohozeav identity the paper is withdrawn. A new draft is prepared with extended existence results for a large class of nonlinearity in arXiv:2504.18907.
♻ ☆ Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
Weican Luo
We study stable regular solutions of the equation $-\operatorname{div}\bigg(\Big(A(x)\nabla u \cdot \nabla u\Big)^{p/2-1}A(x)\nabla u\bigg) = f(u)$ in $B_1 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, where $p > 1$, $f \in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove that stable regular solutions satisfy an interior Hölder estimate for $n < p + 4p/(p - 1)$ when $p \ge 2$, and for $n < 5p$ when $1 < p < 2$. This extends the result of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation. Note that the constant in our Hölder estimate depends on the local $C^1$ norm of $A$, but not on its $C^2$ norm. Our approach is motivated by the interior regularity estimates of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón [7] for the $p$-Laplace equation and by Erneta's [14] treatment of variable coefficients in semilinear elliptic equations.
comment: 60 pages
♻ ☆ Long-time action stability for perturbed KdV near finite-gap tori
Guan Huang
We prove action and spectral stability near finite-gap tori of the periodic Korteweg--de Vries equation under autonomous analytic Hamiltonian perturbations of size $\varepsilon$. The estimates are uniform over prescribed compact families, without small-amplitude or nonresonance assumptions, and allow nearby initial data with infinitely many open gaps. Assuming a strong solution and a uniform higher Sobolev bound on $[0,T_0/\varepsilon]$, we permit one-derivative loss in the perturbing Hamiltonian's normal gradient. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and initial normal Birkhoff size $r_0$, the tangential action variations and weighted sum of normal actions are bounded by $C_δ(r_0^2+\varepsilon^{2δ})$, while the spectral-gap variation in $\ell^2$ is bounded by $C_δ(r_0+\varepsilon^δ)$, for every $0<δ<1/4$. A key ingredient is coercivity of the negative Hessian of the nonlinear KdV Hamiltonian on the full $\ell^2$ action space at every finite-gap action. We combine this with resonance analysis and corrected action observables evaluated along the solution. The hypotheses are verified for several local and nonlocal Hamiltonian perturbations.

☆ Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Hexablock
Sourav Pal, Guicong Su, Nitin Tomar
The hexablock is a domain in $\mathbb{C}^4$ given by \[ \mathbb{H}=\left\{(a,x_1,x_2,x_3)\in \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{E}: \sup_{z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{D}} \left| \frac{a\sqrt{(1-|z_1|^2)(1-|z_2|^2)}} {1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2} \right|<1 \right\}, \] where $\mathbb{E}=\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}: 1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2\neq 0 \ \text{for all}\ z_1,z_2\in\overline{\mathbb D}\right\}$ is the tetrablock. We introduce a Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb H)$ associated with a canonical measure $μ_{\mathbb H}$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathbb H$ of the hexablock. We identify $H^2(\mathbb H)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathbb H,μ_{\mathbb H})$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We prove that $\mathbb H$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $Ψ_{\mathbb H}(\overline{\mathbb D}^4)$, where \[ Ψ_{\mathbb H}(ξ_1, ξ_2,λ_1,λ_2) = \left(\frac{λ_1(ξ_1-1)}{2}, \frac{ξ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \ \frac{λ_1λ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \ ξ_1 ξ_2λ_1λ_2 \right). \] We obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathbb H)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathbb H$-isometries. We characterize $\mathbb H$-unitaries as the images of commuting quadruples of unitaries under $Ψ_{\mathbb H}$ and present a class of $\mathbb H$-contractions from commuting quadruples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^4$ as a spectral set. We prove an analogous characterization of $\mathbb E$-unitaries and present a class of $\mathbb E$-contractions arising from commuting triples of contractions having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set. En route, we also study a weighted Hardy space on the hexablock.

☆ Augmented Dynamical Sampling under unmodeled Forcing
Juan Giribet, Serena Feldberg
We study recovery of an initial state from dynamical samples of a trajectory driven by unknown additive forcing. Measurements against both the original sensors and their images under the adjoint nominal evolution yield one-step residuals that cancel the initial state exactly. These residuals separate forcing estimation from initial-state reconstruction. For a centered Gaussian forcing model with fixed covariance parameters, we combine Gaussian conditioning with canonical dual-frame reconstruction and derive an exact unconditional second-moment identity, including the correlation between the forcing-estimation error and the measurement noise. We also obtain high-probability bounds and identify the irreducible forcing uncertainty through a conditional covariance in the geometry induced by the prior. A hierarchy of augmented sensor systems separates the role of sampling depth in forcing visibility from that of the observation horizon in nominal observability. An image-transport experiment and finite-dimensional and periodic-convolution experiments illustrate the residual correction and the separate roles of sampling depth and observation horizon.
☆ Quantitative characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities
Jaouad Mourtada
The quantitative study of the Gaussian measure of symmetric convex sets is a central theme at the interface of probability theory and convex geometry. From a probabilistic perspective, it amounts to analyzing the tail behavior of suprema of Gaussian processes. The typical magnitude and upper tail of Gaussian processes are well-understood, thanks to Talagrand's celebrated Majorizing Measures theorem and to Gaussian concentration. In contrast, despite fundamental connections with metric entropy established by Kuelbs and Li, no general sharp characterization of the lower tail is available. In this work, we close this gap by establishing a sharp two-sided characterization of Gaussian small ball probabilities, involving both metric entropy and local widths of the underlying convex body. This yields an explicit chaining-type description of lower quantiles of Gaussian processes in terms of the metric structure of the convexified index set, as well as a general comparison inequality for convex sets. We further obtain analogous quantitative characterizations of two important geometric quantities associated with symmetric convex sets, namely intrinsic volumes (quermassintegrals) and the radii of random sections beyond the classical Dvoretzky range. A unifying theme of these results is the central role of convexity in the quantitative understanding of small ball probabilities.
comment: 63 pages
☆ The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
Bonan Chen, Xiang Fang, Feng Guo
We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

☆ Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
Tattwamasi Amrutam, Diptesh Saha, Xumin Wang
We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
comment: 19 pages; preliminary version. Comments are welcome
☆ Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fréchet differentiability
Zhouzhe Wang
We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fréchet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. The associated mismatch scale is stated as a comparison of upper bounds, not as a threshold for the optimal approximation error. Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, error decay with dictionary size, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations. ♻ ☆ The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
Catalin Badea
After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the Polya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the Polya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.

Then we completely characterize the class of conjugations, isometries, and invertible linear operators preserving the shift-invariant subspace structure in terms of weighted composition operators induced by disk automorphisms--combined with the canonical conjugation, isometric multiplication, and invertible Toeplitz operators, respectively. We also establish the existence and non-existence of conjugations that map shift-invariant subspaces to coinvariant subspaces. Finally, we construct a counterexample that rules out an analogous factorization for bounded linear operators preserving shift-invariance of closed images.

We then obtain statistical learning rates for empirical risk minimization with hinge loss over the approximating ReLU neural network classes. For $N$ uniformly distributed samples, the predicted classifiers achieve expected misclassification error of order $N^{-m/(m+n-1)}$ up to an arbitrarily small polynomial loss.

For the endpoint $p=\infty$, we show by a counterexample that the strong convolution inequality fails for the $L_{\infty}$, and we prove that the appropriate endpoint for $p=\infty$ is the martingale $BMO$ space.

While the blow-up rate at non-characteristic points was determined for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ in previous work, the analysis at characteristic points has remained an open problem. The main obstruction is that known constructions of a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables require several steps and rely on a covering argument, which is not available at characteristic points. Focusing on the regime $a < 0$, we construct a Lyapunov functional directly, without any covering argument. This yields uniform bounds on the solution in similarity variables, and hence the blow-up rate at every point, including characteristic ones. To our knowledge, this is the first work to determine the blow-up rate at characteristic points for an equation without scaling invariance.

Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ``mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume as this weak mean value ball has a hole of positive measure.

We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

A locally finite lift on the positive-radius fibres unifies the level-restricted limits at every continuity level. At the macroscopic level, however, the available compactness does not identify a canonical stress-plastic-flow pairing. Moreover, an explicit smooth state satisfying the intrinsic relaxed balance conditions shows that these conditions do not imply macroscopic Prandtl-Reuss normality. It is proven that the constructed dynamics of correlations underlie the description of the evolution of the state, both for finitely and infinitely many particles, governed by the BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density operators or by the hierarchy of nonlinear evolution equations for reduced correlation operators. In fact, it is demonstrated that the behavior of particle correlations governs the dynamics of states in quantum systems with an infinite number of particles.

☆ Boundary-layer detachment and infinite-Reynolds limit of two-dimensional wall-bounded flows
Ciro S. Campolina, Jérémie Bec
Understanding boundary-layer detachment and its consequences for the infinite-Reynolds-number limit remains a major challenge in fluid mechanics. Here, direct numerical simulations of incompressible flow in a two-dimensional periodic channel with no-slip walls are used to investigate this problem. Reynolds-number-dependent initial conditions are constructed with a boundary layer of Prandtl thickness that converge in the energy norm to an analytic, stationary Euler flow, while the associated Prandtl system develops a finite-time singularity. Highly resolved simulations show boundary-layer detachment and departures from Prandtl scaling, yet provide numerical evidence that the Navier--Stokes solutions continue to converge to the Euler flow over the simulated time interval. In particular, the squared energy norm of the velocity difference and the time-averaged energy dissipation both scale approximately as $Re^{-1/2}$, consistently with established convergence criteria. Although the detached vortices become more numerous and intense as the Reynolds number increases, their characteristic size and occupied area appear to decrease. These observations suggest how boundary-layer detachment and the breakdown of the Prandtl description can coexist with convergence to a smooth Euler flow.

☆ The Calderón Problem with Randomly Distributed Resonant Droplets
Anjana E. J., Mourad Sini
We study the recovery of an acoustic coefficient from boundary measurements made after the injection of a collection of small, highly contrasting droplets. This enters into the framework of quantitative ultrasound imaging using contrast agents. The centers are randomly distributed according to a prescribed strictly positive density $ρ\in C^1(\overlineΩ)$. We choose real incident frequencies near an active Newtonian resonance and prove a point-interaction approximation, followed by a comparison with the effective model $(-Δ+P^2ρ-ω^2n^2)u=0$. The constants are uniform as the amplitude $P^2$ increases, provided it is coupled to the size and distribution discrepancy of the droplets. A random rounding and displacement construction verifies the distribution assumption for each such given density. The effective Neumann-to-Dirichlet map is then linearized with a remainder of order $P^{-4}$. We derive reconstruction identities using complex geometrical optics solutions of the known reference operator $-Δ+P^2ρ$. We also estimate the amplification of the boundary-map error in these identities and give a boundary integral correction for reconstruction from the full (and not the linearized) measured map.

Pierre Germain, Simon L. Rydin Myerson, Daniel Pezzi
We study $L^2$ to $L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for the Euclidean Laplacian on the torus in the case where the spectral window is narrow. With a window of constant size this is a classical result of Sogge; in the small-window limit we are left with $L^p$ norms of eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, as considered for instance by Bourgain. For the three-dimensional torus we prove new cases of a previous conjecture of the first two authors concerning the size of these norms; we also refine certain prior results to remove $ε$-losses in all dimensions. We use methods from number theory: the geometry of numbers, the circle method and exponential sum bounds due to Guo. We complement these techniques with height splitting and a bilinear argument to prove sharp results. We exposit on the various techniques used and their limitations.

♻ ☆ Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
Ehsan Mirafzali, Frank Proske, Razvan Marinescu
For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of Röckner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $Φ_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $γ_t = \int_0^t Φ_r Φ_r^{*}\,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are needed. It follows from an integration-by-parts identity on a Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose covering field on Wiener space and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, brought to the equation by the representation $Φ_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$. The linearised theory is carried by $Φ$ and by its own Malliavin derivative $\mathcal{W} = \mathcal{D}Φ$, whose regularity is measured in the time-integrated quadratic energy that the dissipative structure of the linearisation produces, so that no operator norm of the first variation between the spaces of the triple occurs. The stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail; for the latter the dissipative, forcing and exponential-moment hypotheses are established together under trace-class additive noise and a smallness threshold on the noise covariance. A scalar reduction carries the identity beyond the variational class, to the law of a pairing $\langle u(t), \varphi\rangle$ for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, on the same Hölder triangle of moment exponents.
♻ ☆ Small-data $L^2$ theory for the intermediate NLS and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS
Sonae Hadama
In this paper, we study a class of nonlinear Schrödinger equations (NLS) in a unified way. This class includes two important examples: the intermediate NLS (INLS) and the Calogero--Moser derivative NLS (CM-DNLS). Our main results are twofold. First, we prove small-data global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ for a broad class of equations. This includes both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for arbitrary choices of its parameters. Second, we prove small-data scattering in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ under an additional assumption. This result covers both focusing and defocusing CM-DNLS and the INLS for specific choices of its parameters. Both the formulation of the problem, including the notion of solution, and the proofs rely crucially on a linear theory for Schrödinger equations with rough time-dependent potentials. This theory is also of independent interest, since we allow potentials so rough that the standard Duhamel formulation may not make sense. Our approach is perturbative and is built on the bilinear Strichartz estimate proved by Ozawa and Tsutsumi in 1998. In particular, our argument does not rely on integrability.

♻ ☆ The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution

We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.

♻ ☆ Electromagnetic scattering by Minkowski-type bianisotropic media
Manas Kar, Mourad Sini
We consider the time-harmonic scattering of electromagnetic waves by a bounded stationary inclusion whose effective constitutive law is of Minkowski type. The constant vector $V$ is regarded as a constitutive moving parameter. Such a law arises as an effective description of synthetic moving media and of suitable traveling-wave space--time modulations. Starting from the implicit Minkowski relations, we derive a Maxwell transmission system and its Lippmann--Schwinger volume-integral formulation. The dimensionless parameter $β=|V|/c_Ω$ governs the pointwise constitutive inversion, namely the matrix is invertible precisely for $β\neq1$, while on the subcritical branch $0\leqβ<1$ its inverse admits an explicit convergent expansion. Using the algebraic structure of the cross-product operator, we obtain a spectral characterization of solvability and a quantitative sufficient condition separating the static material contrast from the $V$-dependent contribution which allows to justify the convergence of the corresponding Born series. As an application, we prove that full-aperture electric far-field data at a fixed frequency uniquely determine the support of the inclusion within this perturbative regime without assuming that $V$ is known.

The key obstacle is the variable-coefficient coupling $\nabla a\cdot\nabla u$. We show that it is produced by the heat product defect $[P_t(bu)-P_tb\,P_tu]/(2t)$, which converges quantitatively to $\nabla b\cdot\nabla u$. Inserted into a Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, this yields an explicit scheme of depth $O(\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log(1/q))$ whose $\dot H^1$ error is at most $\varepsilon$, uniformly over the coefficient class and $L^2$ data, with all parameters explicit. Each block is controlled in continuum operator norm, without Galerkin truncation. On the torus, band-limited inputs admit an exact pseudo-spectral realization on a grid of $O(1/(\varepsilon a_{\min}))$ points per direction, up to logarithmic and class-dependent factors. The argument extends by carre du champ calculus to strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--Emery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$, with dimension-independent constants after spectral-gap normalization. On the torus we also obtain a $C^2$-type coefficient class and a refinement to Wiener classes of regularity $1+θ$, with product-defect rate $t^{θ/2}$. The factor $1/(2t)$ makes the proved scheme ill-conditioned at small $\varepsilon$.

♻ ☆ Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
Kangsheng Liu
We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders lead to the same total error. They divide this error differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is what we call the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. It can be used to assess the effect of a coarse-mesh correction for nonlinear problems. For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, and the semigroup of the linearized equation has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit exponential stability, Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity, with bounds uniform in the mesh size. The nonlinear solution maps are analytic, also uniformly in the mesh size. These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$.

This paper extends the weak solution theory for the 3D Navier-Stokes equations of Barker, Seregin and Sverak from a critical setting to a supercritical setting making sure to include a useful a priori energy bound as well as a statement about stability under weak-star convergence. Two applications of the a priori bound are then explored. The first provides a spatially local, short-time asymptotic expansion in the time variable starting at $t=0$ which, as a corollary, provides an upper bound on how fast hypothetical non-unique solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations can separate locally. The second establishes higher-order time regularity at a singular time and at spatial points positioned away from the singularity. This quantifies the degree to which the non-local nature of the pressure allows a far flung singularity to disrupt the time regularity at a regular point.

♻ ☆ Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
Leon Bungert, Lucas Schmitt
Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

♻ ☆ Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
Dean Wang
The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $ω_φ(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

Moreover, equality holds if and only if $Ω$ is a ball.

These results hold for first-order as well as for fractional Sobolev mappings. Second, elaborating on the recent preprint of Wang G. and Zhang M. (2026), we derive sharp lower energy bounds for mappings with given Hopf invariant. We apply these bounds to deduce a sufficient energetic condition for the existence of minimizing maps in a given homotopy class. Finally, we exploit this condition, by explicit construction of mappings satisfying it, to prove the existence of energy minimizers from $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{2}$ of Hopf degree $d \in \{\pm2,\pm3,\dotsc,\pm6\}$ and from $\mathbb{S}^{7}$ to $\mathbb{S}^{4}$ of Hopf degree $\pm1$.

In this paper, we consider positive radial entire solutions of nonlinear elliptic equations with bounded positive coefficients and optimize the negative logarithmic derivative of the coefficient. For the scalar equation, we determine the exact, unattained defect threshold and establish quantitative gaps when the coefficient ratio is fixed. Near the threshold, we prove a sharp stability estimate and describe the loss of compactness through a profile decomposition in logarithmic radius, including a characterization of the possible diffuse energy and conditions that exclude it. We also show that the resulting profile configurations can be realized by suitable monotone coefficients. For unequal weighted elliptic systems, we obtain the corresponding sharp defect threshold and fixed-ratio gap, and analyze near-threshold sequences through local homogeneous limits and logarithmic spreading. A BV relaxation and smoothing argument further relates the relaxed and smooth optimization problems.

♻ ☆ Polychromatic Localized Waves with Complex Frequencies in Nonlinear Maxwell Equations with Material Dispersion
Tomas Dohnal, Maximilian Hanisch, Runan He
We study the existence of polychromatic solutions of cubically nonlinear Maxwell equations in the whole space and with dispersive media, i.e., with a time delayed polarization. Due to the complex nature of the dielectric function, the frequencies are complex, resulting in a decay in time. The geometry is that of a waveguide in $x$ with the propagation direction being $y$ and the solutions are localized in $x$ and have a transverse magnetic polarization. These are often referred to as breathers. They are given as a Fourier series in $y$ and $t$ with the leading frequency $ω$ being an eigenvalue of a corresponding operator pencil on $\mathbb{R}$ (in the $x$ variable). Each term in the series corresponds to a different temporal decay rate or a different frequency. The series is constructed iteratively via a sequence of linear ordinary differential equations. Our general result provides the existence under some assumptions on the spectrum and on estimates of the resolvent of the corresponding linear operator. We also produce an example of a waveguide given by the interface of two spatially homogeneous physically relevant media for which these assumptions are satisfied. For such an interface setting the constructed solutions correspond to nonlinear polychromatic surface plasmons.

Simon Coste
This is an expository note on the asymptotics of the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of infinite-dimensional random paths and their common distribution. We present the classical proof for these asymptotics in the case of the Wiener measure, unifying quantization arguments from Dereich and coauthors or Boissard and Le Gouic, and we adapt it for Itô diffusions sampled through the Girsanov theorem. More precisely, let $\mathbb{Q}$ be the law of the solution of a stochastic differential equation with a bounded Lipschitz drift. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ be independent Brownian paths, and let $Z_i$ be their Girsanov weights for $\mathbb{Q}$. The reweighted empirical measure $$\widehatμ_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_iδ_{W_i}}{\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i}$$ approximates $\mathbb{Q}$ when $n$ is large. We prove that the Wasserstein cost $W_p^p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is of order $(\log n)^{-p/2}$, in expectation and almost surely, for every fixed $p\geqslant1$. In the Brownian case where $Z_i=1$ these results show that $\sqrt{\log n}W_p(\widehatμ_n,\mathbb{Q})$ is asymptotically sandwiched between $\sqrt{2λ_d}$ and $4\sqrt{2λ_d}$, where $λ_d$ is the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian operator in the unit ball. We provide numerical experiments to estimate the (conjectured) limiting constant in dimension $d=1$.

The norm formula is stable on $X$ and has the independence property on $W$, and therefore in $\operatorname{Th}(X)$. It is unstable on $Y$ and has no independence property in any model of $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$. Together with $\ell_2$ and $X\oplus_2Y$, these spaces realize all five possible combinations of stability, instability without the independence property, and the independence property on a space with the presence or absence of the independence property in its complete theory. All five spaces are uniformly convex and $\sqrt3$-isomorphic to Hilbert space. Their norms satisfy the common midpoint estimate $\lVert x\rVert,\lVert y\rVert\leq1 \Longrightarrow \lVert(x+y)/2\rVert^2\leq1-(1/12)\lVert x-y\rVert^2$, and $W$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$. The proof for $Y$ uses coordinate truncation and a polynomial bound on threshold patterns for vectors of bounded support. These bounds give finite fat-shattering dimension at each positive scale, from which the complete-theory conclusion follows.

The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.

The motivation is a dyadic series of Castillo, Costin and Costin for the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator: its partial sums are exactly $Q_{2^{-N}}$, so the series is a telescoped rectangle rule. By Poisson summation, on $D(B)$ the error of $Q_T$ is the scalar $T/2$ plus the symmetric limit of the resolvents at the alias points $λ-2πin/T$, $n\ne0$, and the dyadic levels remove these aliases according to the $2$-adic valuation of $n$. If $(S_t)$ belongs to the Crandall--Pazy class with parameter $α\in(0,1]$, that is $\|BS_t\|=O(t^{-1/α})$ as $t\to0$, the error is $O(T^α)$ in operator norm, $O(T^{α+θ})$ on the interpolation space of order $θ$ between $X$ and $D(B)$, and $O(T^{1+α})$ on $D(B)$, the last requiring only resolvent decay of order $α$ along the line $\mathrm{Re}\, z=\mathrm{Re}\,λ$. This interpolates between unitary groups with unbounded generator ($α=0$, no convergence in norm) and analytic semigroups ($α=1$), and every exponent is attained. For smooth data an Euler--Maclaurin expansion justifies Romberg extrapolation. For self-adjoint generators we give closed forms for the contribution of each dyadic level to Stone's formula, and we translate the results into an explicit error bound and step-size rule for Green functions computed from sampled autocorrelations.
