Exploiting the variational structure of the system, the existence of a sharp mass threshold M\textsubscr{c} > 0 is established: all solutions with mass below M\textsubscr{c} are global and bounded, while those with mass above M\textsubscr{c} and sufficiently negative energy are global but blow up in infinite time. Moreover, the value of the critical mass M\textsubscr{c} is related to the best constant of a variant of a Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality.
♻ ☆ Scattering for the KP-II equation
Xi Chen
We prove scattering in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$ for real-valued solutions of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation with localized initial data. The localization is measured in scale-invariant Lorentz or mixed Lebesgue spaces. The admissible data include all real-valued Schwartz functions. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result establishing scattering for the KP-II equation for every real-valued Schwartz initial datum, without any smallness assumption and without the zero mean condition. We also show that some localization is necessary: there are smooth real-valued initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm, with a logarithmic moment, for which the solution does not scatter in $L^2$.
comment: 94 pages. The scattering theorem is extended to more initial data. This version also constructs smooth initial data of arbitrarily small $L^2$ norm whose solutions fail to scatter in $L^2$ in both time directions
♻ ☆ Fujita exponents beyond integrable forcing
Vishvesh Kumar, Mohamed Majdoub
We develop a unified framework for Fujita-type blow-up of solutions to the inhomogeneous semilinear heat equation $$\partial_tu-Δu=|u|^p+\mathbf{w}(x), \qquad (t,x)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad u(0, \cdot)=u_0.$$ The classical integrability assumptions on the forcing term are replaced by quantitative regular variation properties of its spatial mass $$F(R)=\int\limits_{|x|\le R}\mathbf{w}(x)\,dx.$$ Using techniques from regular variation theory together with the Mitidieri--Pohozaev test-function method, we establish sharp Fujita-type nonexistence results and identify the critical exponent in terms of the variation index of $F$. We prove that global solutions do not exist in the subcritical range and obtain critical-case blow-up under suitable slowly varying corrections. The regular variation framework further shows the optimality of the underlying mass condition, extends naturally to anisotropic settings through operator regular variation, and yields sufficient blow-up criteria for sign-changing forcings via the Gaussian-Laplace transform. The approach also applies to space-time dependent forcings, Riesz-potential type forcings, and equations involving the fractional Laplacian, providing a unified description of blow-up thresholds beyond the classical Fujita theory.
comment: The title has been revised, and the presentation has been further enhanced and improved
♻ ☆ A Hadamard Formula for Equilibrium Envelopes under Parallel Deformation
Ziyu Li
Let $(X,ω_0)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $U\Subset X$ have $C^{3,1}$ uniformly strongly pseudoconvex boundary. Consider the signed parallel family $U_t=\{ρ0$ and satisfies the Hadamard formula $$ e'(t)=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{Σ_t}\left(-\partial_{ν_t}u_t\right)^2 dσ_{ρ,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}, |t|<τ. $$ Here $dσ_{ρ,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the interior outward Anzellotti trace of $$ \frac{1}{V} d^cρ\wedge \sum_{p=0}^{n-1}(p+1) ω_{u_t}^{p}\wedgeω_0^{n-1-p}, V=\int_Xω_0^n, ω_{u_t}=ω_0+dd^c u_t. $$ This measure is positive and uniformly comparable to the induced surface measure. The proof combines uniform $C^{1,1}$ estimates up to the boundary from the interior with $1/2$-Hölder stability of the normal derivatives under the normal-flow identifications. We identify the boundary part of the normalized Monge--Ampère measure with the negative outward trace of a divergence-measure flux current. The one-sided weak-* limits of the mixed Bedford--Taylor boundary measures yield the weighted total flux appearing in the variation formula.
comment: 34 pages, 1 figure. Revised exposition and proofs, including clarifications of the boundary densities and uniform regularity estimates; corrected references. Comments are welcome!
♻ ☆ A method of moving planes for a mixed local-nonlocal parabolic equation with quenching
Sergio Junquera, Leandro M. Del Pezzo
In this paper we develop a parabolic version of the method of moving planes on systems with a mixed local and nonlocal diffusion operator, that being $\mathcal{L} = -(-Δ)^s + Δ$, where $(-Δ)^s$ is the integral fractional laplacian. We then use this result to study the quenching phenomena occurring in said systems with a singular absorption term of the type $(1-u)^{-p}$. We prove that there exists a range of multiplicative parameters for which every solution presents quenching, and that for any initial datum $u_0$, there exists a small enough multiplicative parameter such as the solution is globally defined. We also prove that the quenching phenomena cannot happen arbitrarily close to the boundary, but they are contained in a compact subset of the domain.
comment: 26 pages, 2 figures
♻ ☆ Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
Xia Huang, Yuan Li, Yixing Pu
We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=u^{\frac{n+2m}{n-2m}}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if \(\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0\). The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $Δ^2u=u^{\frac{n+4}{n-4}}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-Δu$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.
comment: 52 pages, 2 figures
♻ ☆ An optimal local theory for reaction-diffusion equations driven by non-trace-class noise
Antonio Agresti, Fabian Germ, Mark Veraar
We study local well-posedness for a class of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations driven by multiplicative, possibly colored, noise. The interaction between rough stochastic forcing and polynomial nonlinearities naturally leads to solutions with low spatial regularity, making the treatment of the nonlinear terms delicate. Our main contribution is a general local existence and uniqueness theory for SPDEs with rough noise and highly irregular initial data. The framework also yields new results in standard noise regimes, including trace-class noise and space-time white noise. We identify the critical initial-data spaces for a wide range of nonlinearities, and we establish instantaneous parabolic regularization, general blow-up criteria, and sufficient conditions for positivity preservation. We apply the abstract theory to several prototypical models, including the stochastic Allen-Cahn, Burgers, Fisher-KPP, and coupled Gray-Scott equations. Finally, in the one-dimensional space-time white-noise setting, we combine our local theory with existing global a priori results in a highly singular regime.
comment: 50 pages; Corrected some mistakes and typographical errors identified with the assistance of LLM
♻ ☆ Regularity of Lipschitz free boundaries for weak solutions of Alt-Caffarelli type problems
Joan Domingo-Pasarin, Xavier Ros-Oton
Motivated by the Serrin problem, we study weak solutions of the generalised Alt-Caffarelli problem $-Δu = f$ in $Ω$, $u = 0$ on $\partialΩ$, $\partial_νu = Q$ on $\partialΩ$. Our main result establishes that if $Ω$ is Lipschitz, then it is actually $C^{\infty}$ (provided that $f$ and $Q$ are smooth). This was known before only for viscosity solutions. As a corollary, we obtain an alternative solution of Serrin's problem in the case of Lipschitz domains. We also discuss the characterisation of the regularity of Lipschitz domains in terms of their Poisson kernel.
comment: Version changes: we added the missing hypothesis Q > 0 in Theorem 1.4
♻ ☆ Existence of two-dimensional deep capillary solitary water waves with constant vorticity
James Rowan, Lizhe Wan
We consider two-dimensional capillary water waves with nonzero constant vorticity in infinite depth. We first derive the Babenko equation that describes the profile of the solitary wave. When the velocity $c$ is close to a critical velocity, the Babenko equation can be reduced to the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation plus perturbative error. This gives the existence of small-amplitude solitary wave solutions for the water wave system with constant vorticity whose profiles are close to solutions of the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
comment: 30 pages, title changed
♻ ☆ Global compactness results for fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy Sobolev operator on a bounded domain
Nirjan Biswas
In this paper, we establish a Struwe type global compactness result for a class of nonlinear critical Hardy-Sobolev exponent problems driven by the fractional $p$-Laplace Hardy-Sobolev operator.
comment: 18 pages
♻ ☆ Partition-of-Unity Gaussian Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
Amir Noorizadegan
Gaussian basis functions provide an efficient and flexible alternative to spline activations in Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs), but their performance is sensitive to the Gaussian scale parameter ε. We introduce the partition-of-unity Gaussian KAN (PU-GKAN), a kernel-based normalization framework that transfers the Shepard partition-of-unity principle to trainable KAN edge functions. Each Gaussian edge basis is normalized by its local sum over fixed centers, preserving the standard edge-based architecture and essentially the same trainable coefficient structure as GKAN. The resulting feature map reproduces constants exactly at the edge level and admits an explicit normalized finite-feature kernel interpretation. Numerical experiments show that PU-GKAN reduces sensitivity to ε, improves validation accuracy for most smooth and moderately non-smooth targets, and provides more stable training behavior. These benefits persist across variations in sample size and number of centers, higher-dimensional architectures, and Matern RBF bases. PU-GKAN also improves physics-informed neural networks for Helmholtz and wave equations, with validation-error reductions of up to 90%. These results establish partition-of-unity normalization as a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework for improving the reliability and accuracy of radial basis function KANs.
♻ ☆ On the Stokes conjecture for compressible gravity waves of extreme form
Lili Du, Chunlei Yang
In 1880, G. G. Stokes [Mathematical and Physical Papers, Vol.I] examined an extreme two-dimensional irrotational periodic traveling water wave under the influence of gravity and conjectured a symmetric corner of \(120^\circ\) at the crest. The conjecture was first proved rigorously by Amick, Fraenkel, and Toland [Acta Math. 148 (1982)] and, independently, by Plotnikov [Dinamika Sploshn. Sredy 57 (1982)] via the Nekrasov integral equation. In the early 2010s, Varvarua and Weiss [Acta Math. 206 (2011)] revisited the conjecture by introducing a novel geometric method, which provided an affirmative answer to the conjecture without requiring the structural assumptions used in earlier works, such as the isolation of the stagnation points and the symmetry and monotonicity of the free surface. The main purpose of this paper is to establish the validity of the Stokes conjecture in the context of compressible gravity water waves. More precisely, we prove that, at each stagnation point of a compressible gravity water wave, a sharp crest with an included angle of \(120^\circ\) forms, which gives the first rigorous confirmation of the compressible counterpart of the classical Stokes conjecture of 1880. The central aspect of our approach is the discovery of a new monotonicity formula and a modified version of it for quasilinear free boundary problems of Bernoulli type. Another key ingredient is a new nonlinear frequency formula, which we combine with the concentration-cancellation theory of Evans and Muller [J. Amer. Math. Soc. 7 (1994)]. These newly developed monotonicity formulas are valid for nonlinear problems and enable us to carry out a blow-up analysis at each stagnation point and to provide a complete classification of the blow-up limits near each stagnation point.
comment: 95 Pages. This revision corrects typos and an erroneous estimate from the previous version. The results are strengthened
♻ ☆ A Trichotomy for Modified Scattering Across the Yukawa-Coulomb Transition
Yonggeun Cho, Jinyeop Lee
We study the long-time asymptotics of the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Yukawa potential \[ V_μ(x)=\frac{e^{-μ|x|}}{|x|}, \qquad 0\leqμ\leq1. \] The Coulomb case corresponds to $μ=0$, while $μ>0$ introduces the screening length $μ^{-1}$. In the limit $μ\to0$ and $t\to\infty$, the asymptotic behavior depends on the comparison between the observation scale $t$ and the screening length $μ^{-1}$, equivalently on the parameter $μt$. This leads to three distinct asymptotic regimes, according as $μt\to0$, $μt\to L\in(0,\infty)$, or $μt\to\infty$, with different modified scattering phases in each case.
comment: Corrected minor errors, simplified the notation and organization
♻ ☆ Uniform dispersive estimates for the semi-classical Hartree equation with long-range interaction
Sonae Hadama
In this paper, we consider the Hartree equation with smooth but long-range interaction in the semi-classical regime, in three-dimensional space. We show that the density function of a small-data solution decays at the optimal rate. When the semi-classical parameter $\hbar \in (0,1]$ is fixed, our result is essentially covered by the recent work by Nguyen and You; however, the novelty of this paper is the uniformity with respect to $\hbar$. Namely, both the smallness condition for the initial data and the bounds for the solution are independent of $\hbar$. Our proof relies on three main ingredients. First, we prove the boundedness of finite-time wave operators modified by phase corrections. Second, we show an $L^1$--$L^\infty$ dispersive estimate for the modified propagator. Third, we give various kinds of commutator estimates for density operators. By combining them, we can apply the usual bootstrap argument to obtain the main result.
comment: 64 pages
♻ ☆ Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
Dean Wang
The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $ω_φ(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
♻ ☆ Non-uniqueness for the Complex Ginzburg-Landau Equation
Joel Dahne, Vladimír Šverák
We show that singularities of the three-dimensional cubic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation developing from smooth initial data can induce non-uniqueness of solutions after the time of blowup. The solutions we study start as backward self-similar solutions, and the source of the non-uniqueness is an unstable eigenvalue of the linearization around the forward self-similar profile generated by the singularity. We establish the existence of this eigenvalue, and hence the non-uniqueness, by a computer-assisted proof for specific values of the parameters in the equation. The work is in part motivated by similarities to conjectured behavior for the Navier-Stokes equation, with which the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation shares several important properties, such as an energy inequality and the scaling symmetry.
comment: 63 pages, 4 figures
♻ ☆ Linear Asymptotic Stability of the Smooth 1-Solitons for the Degasperis-Procesi Equation
Simon Deng, Mathew A. Johnson, Stéphane Lafortune
In this paper, we study the asymptotic stability of smooth 1-solitons in the Degasperis-Procesi (DP) equation. Such solutions necessarily exist on a non-zero background, and their spectral and orbital stability has previously been verified by Li, Liu & Wu and by Lafortune & Pelinovsky. Using the complete integrability of the DP equation to establish the strong spectral stability of smooth solitary waves, namely that the origin is the only eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and that, moreover, in appropriate exponentially weighted spaces the non-zero spectrum for the linearized operator admits a spectral gap away from the imaginary axis. This spectral gap result {is then} upgraded to an exponential decay estimate on the semigroup associated with the linearized operator, establishing a linear asymptotic stability result in exponentially weighted spaces. Finally, we outline analytical challenges with extending our result to the nonlinear level.
comment: 44 pages, 2 figures. Correcting typos, adding additional exposition
♻ ☆ The doubling property of the elliptic measure, for elliptic operators with drifts satisfying an average diverging condition
Aritro Pathak
We show doubling of the elliptic measure corresponding to the operator with an elliptic principal term and a drift that diverges, on average on Whitney cubes, like the inverse distance to the boundary, with a small constant. Essentially a small Carleson constant assumption on the drift, this generalizes earlier results with the hypothesis of pointwise smallness of such a drift. This relates to recent perturbative results of rough Dirichlet solvability in domains with drifts or potentials that satisfy a Carleson measure condition, which have also been considered earlier by Hofmann-Lewis and Kenig-Pipher. While we work in 1-sided chord arc domains, these results are new even for the half-space. In the process, we also prove Hardy inequalities in such domains with Alhfors-David regular boundary, using a stopping time argument.
comment: Corrected a minor error with addition of Lemma 6
Functional Analysis
☆ Extensions from Positive and Full Unit Spheres of $C^\infty([0,1])$ with a Compatible Fréchet Metric
Min-Ruei Lin
We study isometric extensions from positive and full unit spheres of $C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb F)$, where $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. We equip these spaces with a translation-invariant metric that induces the usual Fréchet topology, is unbounded, has convex balls, and has strictly increasing distances from zero along nonzero rays. Every surjective isometry of the pointwise positive unit sphere extends uniquely to a complex-linear surjective isometry of the complex-valued space. Restriction gives the unique real-linear isometric extension on the real-valued space. On the full unit sphere, every surjective isometry extends uniquely to a real-linear surjective isometry. The positive-sphere maps are compositions with the identity or an admissible reflection. The full-sphere maps also allow constant unimodular factors and, over the complex field, conjugation. We also classify the surjective ambient isometries. A counterexample shows that these metric properties alone do not guarantee positive-sphere extension. Under an explicit anchor condition, we classify surjective isometries of finite-order jet-positive spheres for maximum-type anchored metrics and prove that they extend uniquely to complex-linear surjective isometries. The classification allows any permutation of the anchored coordinates, combined with the identity or reflection on the highest-derivative component. The condition holds for every anchor when $m=1$ or $m=2$.
comment: 33 pages
☆ Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
Shuaibing Luo, Eskil Rydhe
Let $\mathcal H$ be a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal H$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal H$ is concave, then $\mathcal H$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick space. This gives an affirmative answer to the concavity part of Shimorin's question \cite{Sh02} and extends his theorem on the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property of Dirichlet-type spaces with superharmonic weights.
☆ Separable $\mathcal L_{\infty}$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$
Jesús Suárez
We construct separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$, which, to the best of our knowledge, are the first known examples of this kind. Our technique employs the Bourgain--Pisier construction and a quantitative analysis of metric types in limits of finite-dimensional $η$-admissible embeddings. The argument rests on two complementary estimates: approximate radial centres yield asymptotic separation of tree increments, while an admissibility inequality yields asymptotic gain, leading to concentration on Kalton's interlacing graphs. This leads to an abstract criterion for property $Q$ in terms of asymptotic separation $AS_θ$ and asymptotic gain $AG_α$. We illustrate the limitations of this criterion with Johnson--Lindenstrauss spaces. Our examples exclude uniform embeddings of the unit ball of $c_0$, strengthening in a nonlinear direction the classical Bourgain--Delbaen phenomenon. As an application, every separable Banach space embeds isometrically into a separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-space whose unit ball is not a uniform retract of the unit ball of its bidual.
comment: 39 pages
☆ On Solvability of Irregular Infinite-Dimensional Differential-Algebraic Equations
Ala' Alalabi, Lorena Bociu, Birgit Jacob, Kirsten Morris
This paper investigates the solvability of infinite-dimensional differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) on Hilbert spaces. We focus on irregular systems for which the operator pencil is not surjective onto the full state space, but only onto a subspace determined by the algebraic constraints. We establish a Lumer-Phillips-type generation result for this class of systems, showing that dissipativity together with a partial surjectivity condition yields a contraction semigroup on the dynamic subspace. The resulting wellposedness conditions are compared with existing solvability results. We further extend the analysis to systems in which hidden algebraic constraints restrict the dynamics to a proper closed subspace of the dynamical subspace. Under an additional structural condition, we show that the resulting constrained system is $E$-radial on suitably chosen spaces. We also demonstrate that semigroup generation does not, in general, imply $E$-radiality on the original state spaces. This provides a Weierstraß-type decomposition useful for controller design. The framework is illustrated by some examples.
☆ The vector-valued Stein inequality and dimension-free R-sectoriality
Jan van Neerven

For each family, the dimension-free \(R\)-bound of the resolvents on the negative real axis equals the Stein constant. Consequently, the resolvent estimate on the negative real axis already implies uniform \(R\)-sectoriality at an angle strictly smaller than \(π/2\). We furthermore prove that the full and dyadic Stein properties are equivalent and that they are independent of the exponent \(1
comment: 29 pages, 1 figure
☆ Twisted convolution with conic support and the parabolic algebra
Jie Qin
We prove that tempered distributions on \(\mathbb R^{2n}\) whose supports satisfy a common strict cone condition form a unital associative algebra without zero divisors under twisted convolution \(\star\). The supports may be noncompact, and the associated Weyl maps need not be bounded. As applications, we show that the parabolic algebra and the norm-closed algebra generated by positive translations and modulations have no zero divisors, confirming Levene's conjecture. We also obtain a zero-product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the one-dimensional Fock space with bounded symbols whose distributional Fourier transforms satisfy a common strict cone condition. The proof of the distribution theorem uses Schwartz smoothing between distributional Weyl maps to convert a hypothetical zero product of nonzero distributions into a smooth function \(h\not\equiv0\) satisfying the same cone condition and \(h\star h=0\). The cone bound implies the \(Q\)-support condition, meaning that some linear functional is bounded above on \(\operatorname{supp}h\) and has compact upper level sets there. Truncating \(h\) near the maximum of this functional and applying the support identity for compactly supported twisted squares rule out \(h\star h=0\). For the operator applications, uniformly bounded Weyl-conjugation averages identify twisted convolution with bounded operator composition under the common cone condition.
comment: 64 pages
☆ Gelfand and sampling numbers of weighted Wiener spaces
Moritz Moeller
The aim of this paper is to establish sharp asymptotic bounds on the Gelfand numbers of weighted Wiener spaces $\mathcal{A}^r_θ$ measured in $L_q$. This is done by using results for Gelfand numbers of sequence spaces and applying them to each layer of a hyperbolic cross to obtain results for Gelfand numbers between different (weighted) Wiener spaces. These can then be used to establish bounds in $L_q$ by combining them with known results and techniques for Besov spaces. This significantly narrows a gap in the current research, since the Gelfand numbers provide a lower bound on the (non-linear) sampling numbers, whereas upper bounds on this quantity have been studied in multiple papers via an upper bound given by the best m-term approximation.
☆ Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity
Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher
We construct quantum channels by averaging unitary shift conjugations with respect to $κ$-additive probability measures on measurable abelian groups. The channels act on the duals of operator algebras generated by shifts and bounded measurable multiplication operators. They preserve $κ$-additivity of quantum states and admit a weak-$*$ integral representation on this class. If the averaging measure vanishes on singletons, every output state is singular. In the appendix, we also establish the corresponding Fubini's theorem for $κ$-additive measures.
comment: 13 pages, 1 figure
☆ Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
Trung Hoa Dinh
For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.
☆ An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
Ahmed A. Abdelhakim
Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.
☆ The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
Emanuel Milman
We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $λ$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.
comment: 18 pages
☆ Vector metrics with values in pre-Riesz spaces I: transfer of order convergence along vector lattice covers
Cüneyt Çevik
Vector metric spaces in the sense of Çevik and Altun take values in a vector lattice, but their axioms use only the order of the value space. We develop the theory for vector metrics with values in an Archimedean pre-Riesz space $E$, i.e.\ an ordered vector space admitting a bipositive order dense embedding $i$ into a vector lattice $Y$. We ask when an $E$-valued vector metric $d$ and the vector-lattice-valued metric $i\circ d$ have the same convergent and Cauchy nets and sequences. Relatively uniform convergence transfers along every cover. For nets, $\mathrm{o}_3$-convergence transfers if and only if the cover has an intrinsic domination property. This property holds for pervasive covers, by a result of Kalauch and van Gaans, for uniformly dense covers and in finite dimensions; it fails for an example of Kalauch and van Gaans. Sequential convergence transfers under a countable domination property implied by uniform density, but not under pervasiveness. For uncountable $Γ$, the vector lattice $\mathbb{R}\mathbf 1\oplus c_{00}(Γ)$ is pervasive in its Dedekind completion $\ell^\infty(Γ)$ without the transfer, while for countable $Γ$ the transfer holds; the difference is explained by order separability. In finite dimensions, with a closed generating cone, all these convergences coincide with norm convergence in every cover. For $C^1[0,1]$-valued integral metrics, positivity of the kernel on the diagonal forces all order convergences to coincide with $L^1$-convergence. For the Volterra kernel $(t-s)_+$, by contrast, $L^1$-convergence, relatively uniform convergence and order convergence are pairwise different, and we describe each explicitly.
☆ Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
Cüneyt Çevik
A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $σ$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.

Janko Bračič, Marko Kandić

We characterize nonemptiness of $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ in terms of orthogonal idempotents, compute $d_σ(\mathscr A)$ for finite-dimensional algebras, and show that every class $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ is open. For operators on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ these classes are dense in $\mathscr B(X)$, which implies that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr B(X))$ is a dense $G_δ$-subset of $\mathscr B(X)$. By contrast, we exhibit a commutative Banach algebra whose spectral classes are all nonempty and none of which is dense. For self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, we obtain sharper perturbation results, with positive semi-definite perturbations of prescribed rank producing spectra with exactly $n$ components. We show that a quasinilpotent weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $X$ admits a nilpotent rank-one operator $F$ such that the spectrum of $S_w+αF$ has infinitely many components for every nonzero $α$.

The classical Whitney theorem on real-analytic approximation is a fundamental result in finite-dimensional analysis and geometry. Extending this theory to general infinite-dimensional Banach spaces involves longstanding open problems. This paper is the first part of our study of Whitney-type real-analytic approximation on Banach spaces, focusing on the $C^0$ and $C^1$ cases. We prove that a real Banach space admits a separating polynomial if and only if it admits a polynomial topological embedding into a real Hilbert space. We also introduce classes of mappings that locally factor through polynomial maps into finite-dimensional spaces and develop methods of real-analytic approximation for these classes. Using these tools, we establish fine $C^0$ and $C^1$ real-analytic approximation theorems for broad classes of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As applications, we resolve several open problems, including those concerning Whitney-type extensions with real analyticity off closed sets, real-analytic approximation preserving Lipschitz constants, and the real-analytic equivalence of diffeomorphic open subsets of Hilbert spaces.

We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.

Meanwhile, we derive trace formulas for corresponding operators, which cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by formally replacing the dimension parameter with infinity. We prove that $μ_{X_1+X_2}$ has no singular continuous part, that its density is strictly positive on this open set, and we determine the masses of its atoms. Explicit calculations are possible in several important cases. As an application, we combine our Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula with known subordination convergence results to calculate the limiting logarithmic potentials of free multiplicative random walks. The theoretical developments are illustrated with explicit examples using different types of weighted shifts and applied to quantum mechanical models, including a detailed treatment of the Weyl algebra and its Schrödinger representation.

For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. For a convex body $K \subset \mathbb R^d$ let $Δ(K)$ be the expected distance between two independent uniform points of $K$, and let $θ(K)$ be the corresponding expectation for normalized surface measure on $\partial K$. ♻ ☆ On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
Michael Hinz, Jonas M. Tölle, Lauri Viitasaari
We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are Hölder curves or Hölder parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.

Analogs for integer-valued monotone log-concave random variables are also obtained. Our main tools are decreasing rearrangement, majorization, and the change of measure.

The Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits (KLS) conjecture asserts that isotropic log-concave probability measures have Poincaré constants bounded by a universal constant, independently of dimension. In this work, we provide a deterministic variational proof that the Poincaré constant $C_P(μ)\le25$, where $μ$ is any isotropic log-concave probability measure. The proof centers on mean-zero integration of compatible symmetric tensor fields. Starting from constant tensors, we obtain factorially normalized Appell polynomials by iterating this procedure. Using moment estimates and a quadratic variance inequality, we establish geometric bounds on these iterated primitives through a \emph{joint} variational argument over the measure and test function. At a maximizing pair, stationarity in the test function controls the weighted sum of the two highest-order cumulant terms arising from the measure variation. To extend these bounds to arbitrary compatible fields, we use a weighted Helmholtz--Hodge decomposition of weighted divergence, the formal adjoint of differentiation. Controlling the curl in the decomposition yields a curvature comparison for the integration operators, uniformly in tensor order. Combining this comparison with the Appell bounds gives a bound on the full integration operator and hence the stated Poincaré inequality. The estimate is independent of the auxiliary positive curvature, allowing approximation to general isotropic log-concave measures.

We establish a two-mode stability theory for Monge solutions of the multi-marginal optimal transport problem with barycentric quadratic cost. The associated tuple of maps splits into an external barycentric mode and internal relative modes. A quadratic lower bound for the Kantorovich defect controls the internal modes and yields a square-root estimate without invoking any two-marginal map-stability theorem. The external mode is the optimal transport map from the fixed source to the Wasserstein barycenter. Combining the resulting two-mode estimate with Mérigot's sharp theorem gives a $\frac{1}{4}$-Hölder estimate for general perturbations, while barycenter-preserving perturbations satisfy a $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder estimate. We prove that both exponents and the dependence on the weights are optimal. We also examine the scope of such decomposition beyond the barycentric cost: collective-coordinate perturbations and uniformly concave costs of the sum retain the two-mode estimate, whereas the analyses of graph interactions, hedonic costs, and translation-invariant costs identify the two possible obstructions -- loss of relative coercivity and lack of stability for the remaining external modes.

♻ ☆ A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas
We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain the complete bound $2$, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.

☆ Local well-posedness for viscous heat-conducting fluids with discontinuous densities
Francesco Fanelli, M. Eugenia Martínez-Martini
In this paper, we consider the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in space dimension $d\geq2$. We prove local well-posedness of solutions having density only in $L^p\cap L^\infty$, for suitable $p\in\,]1,+\infty[\,$, with no further regularity requirements. In particular, our result yields existence and uniqueness of solutions in the case of discontinuous densities presenting a jump across a smooth interface. The existence proof is based on the use of the Hoff effective viscous flux and on a combination of both maximal regularity and Chemin's striated regularity arguments. Uniqueness, under the assumption of slightly more regular initial velocity fields and temperatures, relies on a Lagrangian approach, supplemented with an original bootstrap argument which shows improved time integrability properties of the solution.

Ben B. J. Siriki, N'Guessan F. Alla, Adama Coulibaly
In this paper, we investigate the effect of a fixed time delay on the internal stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam clamped at one end with distributed damping. Under appropriate assumptions on the feedback weights, we first establish that the problem is well-posed using semigroup theory. Furthermore, using the multiplier method combined with a suitable Lyapunov functional, we prove the exponential stability of the system.
☆ Exponential stabilization of an Euler--Bernoulli beam via internal feedback under distributed time delay
Ben B. J. Siriki, Droh A. Behi, N'Guessan F. Alla, Adama Coulibaly
In this paper, we investigate the internal stabilization of a closed-loop system which consists of an Euler--Bernoulli beam subjected to a structural damping mechanism with a distributed delay into the domain. Under appropriate assumptions on the weights of the delay term and internal damping, we first prove the well-posedness of the system by a semigroup approach. Then, by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov functional and utilizing the multiplier method, we establish the exponential decay of the system energy.

Mohameden Ahmedou, Ruben Jakob
We study endpoints and conformal projection of the Möbius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichmüller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

Diaraf Seck
Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded domain, with boundary homeomorphic to a sphere, carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; for such domains it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem valid in every dimension $N\ge2$: if the eigenfunction $u$ stays strictly below its boundary value $c>0$, then $kR^*\ge j_{N/2,1}$, where $k^2$ is the eigenvalue, $R^*$ the radius of the ball of equal volume and $j_{N/2,1}$ the first positive zero of $J_{N/2}$; equality holds only for the ball. We compare this threshold with the unconditional bound $kR^*\ge 2^{1/N}j_{N/2-1,1}$ given by the Krahn--Szegő inequality. Using Payne's P-function $P=|\nabla u|^2+λu^2$ we prove that every Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u|>\sqrt N\,|c|$, together with pointwise and distance bounds. We correct the shape-optimization approach of an earlier work by computing the optimality condition of the associated boundary functional with an adjoint state. Using the transcendence of the zeros of Bessel functions of integer and half-integer order, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the ball, in every dimension, both for the Schiffer problem and for the Berenstein problem. Finally, we reconstruct numerically the convex four-dimensional counterexample of Guo and check the above statements on it.

We first show that the vanishing of the material derivative on the boundary, assumed in~\cite{Se24}, never holds, and we compute the correct optimality condition, involving an adjoint state, for the associated functional $J_2$. We prove that every planar Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u| > \sqrt{2}|c|.$ Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem: if $u < c$ in $Ω$ , then $kR^* \geq j_{1,1},$ where $R^*$ is the radius of the disc of equal area, and equality holds only for the disc. The three-dimensional remainder has small energy, prescribed second-derivative bounds for density and velocity, and a prescribed first-derivative bound for temperature. Its initial temperature lies in a fixed positive interval; its second derivatives need only be finite. A unique global positive strong solution and algebraic decay in the uniform norm are obtained. The wave-strength threshold depends on lower-order planar bounds, while the allowed remainder size may depend on the complete planar datum.

The stability of viscous contact waves is established for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations under large integrable perturbations. A unique global positive solution is obtained, which converges uniformly to a fixed Eulerian contact profile at the optimal inverse square-root rate in time. The wave-strength threshold depends only on bounds for the initial density perturbation in the first-order Sobolev norm, the energy of the initial velocity perturbation, the thermal relative entropy and the total conserved excess, together with positive lower bounds for the initial density and temperature. It is independent of higher Sobolev norms and the common far-field velocity. No square-integrability condition is imposed on the initial anti-derivatives. Derivative and pressure decomposition estimates are also established for the evolving solution.

Accounting for the degeneracy that is induced by phase invariance and possible additional neutral directions, we establish a universal lower bound of order $κ^2$ for the inverse coercivity constant $ρ_u(κ)$ of local minimizers with uniformly bounded Hessian kernel dimension. For nonvanishing states that satisfy a quantitative subcriticality condition, we prove a matching upper bound, showing that the quadratic scaling is sharp. On a fixed annulus with a fixed smooth magnetic potential, we then construct nonvanishing local minimizers for which $ρ_u(κ)\simeqκ^4$. Moreover, we exhibit branches of strictly stable local minimizers along which the inverse coercivity constant diverges as stability is lost. Consequently, no locally bounded upper estimate depending only on $κ$ can hold uniformly over all phase-nondegenerate local minimizers, even for a fixed domain and magnetic potential.

In each fundamental period $T_ε$, the trace has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate minimum and a nondegenerate maximum. The period and the solution centered at the trace minimum and rescaled to period one depend smoothly on $ε$. As $ε\to 0$, $T_ε= \frac{4}{n-2}\log(1/ε)+O(1)$. As $ε\to 1$, the solutions converge to the cylindrical solution and their periods tend to that of its linearized oscillation. If the exterior and inclusion boundaries are $C^{2,β}$, we also obtain a global Lipschitz estimate, uniform in $\varepsilon$, for compatible $C^{0,σ}$ tractions, where $0<σ<β$. The displacement is normalized modulo rigid motions, and the estimate controls the full gradient in the matrix and the inclusions. The boundary argument uses a local Neumann comparison estimate whose constant is independent of the choice of inclusions retained in cells cut by an artificial localization boundary. We prove this estimate by combining cellwise rigidification, divergence-free stress extensions, and duality, and then apply a boundary Campanato iteration and local estimates at the microscopic scale.

Their time and transverse spatial derivatives decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/2}$, measured in $\Hm(\R^3)$ for the conservative perturbation and in $H^1(\R^3)$ for the primitive perturbation.} No zero-mass condition or spectral stability assumption is imposed. On the whole space $\R^3$, the main analytical difficulties stem from the continuous transverse low frequencies, the opposite signs of shock compression in $L^2(\R^3)$ and unweighted $\Hm(\R^3)$, and the absence of density dissipation in the continuity equation coupled with temperature variations. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce a density-weighted $\Hm(\R^3)$ multiplier built from the inverse entropy Hessian and a modified curl operator. Through entropy symmetrization and the curl projection, all second-order acoustic derivatives of the potential cancel out and the transverse acoustic modes are controlled, so that the normal Euler drift is governed by the compressive derivative of the characteristic speed. Combined with an effective momentum variable and a momentum--density cross estimate, this negative-order energy absorbs the unfavorable compression term in the $L^2$ energy and closes the $H^3(\R^3)$ a priori estimates without loss of derivatives.

We compare two heat flows for the same corotational map of a disk into a warped product of two spheres, with the same fixed boundary values. The ordinary harmonic map heat flow develops a singularity in finite time. When the domain metric is instead determined by the critically normalized Green potential of the current energy distribution, the solution exists for all time. Two harmonic spheres of energy $4π$ form at separated scales, in addition to a nonconstant harmonic root. The energy and the image diameter of the necks tend to zero without restriction to a sequence of times. The main estimate controls the difference between the inner source mass and its critical value by the weighted tension. This is necessary because that difference is integrated over a neck of unbounded logarithmic length. Along a sequence of times the Green metric on the middle neck is asymptotically cylindrical after a spatially constant normalization.

A first-moment decomposition isolates the slow modes, and Gaussian resolvent bounds are transferred to polynomially weighted spaces. This yields nonlinear stability with the endpoint exponential decay rate $(1-λ)/2$, where $λ$ denotes the strain asymmetry, without any additional polynomial factor in time. We identify this limit as the value of a zero-sum stopping game whose zero set determines the Wulff shape. This zero set coincides with that of the positive part of the value function of an unconstrained optimal control problem if and only if Freidlin's condition holds. When Freidlin's condition fails, we derive a pointwise characterization of the stopping-game zero set, yielding a convex hull representation. These results then yield explicit Wulff shapes and directional spreading speeds for all habitat speed. As the habitat speed increases, the Wulff shape evolves from a large ball to a truncated ball. It then develops conical, cylindrical, and paraboloidal boundary components attached to spherical parts, before eventually becoming a smaller ball. Some of these geometric transitions occur while both axial spreading speeds remain unchanged. We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.

In this work, we take a step towards understanding overdamped Langevin dynamics for the minimization of a general class of objective functions $\mathcal{L}$. We establish well-posedness and regularity of the law $ρ_t$ of the process through novel a priori estimates, and, very importantly, we characterize the large-time behavior of $ρ_t$ under truly minimal assumptions on $\mathcal{L}$. In the case of integrable Gibbs density, the law converges to the normalized Gibbs measure. In the non-integrable case, we prove that the law diffuses. The rate of convergence, in terms of relative Dirichlet energy with respect to the Gibbs measure, is $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$, where $σ$ is the diffusion parameter. Under a Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition on $\mathcal{L}$, we also derive sharp exponential contractivity results toward the set of global minimizers. Combining these results we provide the first systematic convergence analysis of Langevin dynamics under PL conditions in non-integrable Gibbs settings: a first phase of exponential in time contraction toward the set of minimizers and then a large-time exploration over it with rate $\mathcal O(1/(σt))$ in terms of the relative Dirichlet energy.

The resulting structure gives rise to the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm (ILCA). Lexicographic confinement and singular-transition skipping restrict the candidate domain, whereas RRPEF reuse and scalar-equivalent transition bypassing avoid redundant Gauss--Jordan reductions while retaining the corresponding basic-solution tableaux. Strict lexicographic progression prevents cycling, while the traversal proceeds independently of objective improvement under degeneracy-induced stalling. ILCA terminates when a feasible tableau satisfies the standard optimality conditions and otherwise completes the finite traversal, including for Tucker- and Cunningham-type totally degenerate configurations.

☆ Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
Durvudkhan Suragan
We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

In this paper, we provide a comprehensive study of how the classical Black--Scholes-type market framework behaves in an infinite-dimensional setting. The asset prices are modeled by stochastic evolution equations in a separable Hilbert space. The evolution of the risk-free asset and the corresponding discounting operators are governed by a strongly continuous group of bounded linear operators. Accordingly, we consider contingent claims with Hilbert-space-valued payoffs, whose values are discounted through the corresponding operators. Within this framework, we investigate the pricing and hedging of contingent claims, deriving the corresponding Hilbert-space-valued Black--Scholes equations and establishing exact replication results for both strong and mild solutions. We also study the special case where the infinitesimal generator is given by $A=rI$, allowing for real-valued contingent claims. We further investigate no-arbitrage and market completeness, introducing a Hilbert lattice structure to formulate arbitrage and characterizing attainability through operator equations associated with martingale representations. We also establish asymptotic completeness through finite-dimensional noise truncations. We introduce geometric Brownian motions in Hilbert spaces and derive sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an equivalent risk-neutral measure, together with explicit pricing formulas for some tractable examples. These results extend key aspects of the classical Black--Scholes framework to markets with infinite-dimensional asset-price dynamics. As a concrete application, the model can be interpreted as a segmented market consisting of a sequence of one-dimensional geometric Brownian motions.

☆ On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
Mikhail Anikushin
We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.
☆ Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
Gabriel Larotonda, Tin-Yau Tam
An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.

Heinz H. Bauschke, Tran Thanh Tung
Firmly nonexpansive operators arise naturally as resolvents of monotone operators and as generalizations of projections and proximal mappings in convex optimization and fixed point theory. While their iterates are known to converge weakly to a fixed point, strong convergence is not guaranteed (Genel and Lindenstrauss, 1975). Strong convergence of Cesàro means of iterates is also known to fail for general nonlinear nonexpansive mappings (Krengel and Lin, 1987). In this paper, we show that this failure persists in the much smaller class of firmly nonexpansive mappings. Using suitable meshes, we construct a new explicit family of counterexamples in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with the origin as the unique fixed point. In the harmonic case, the Cesàro means of the iterates remain bounded away from the origin. Another variant yields Cesàro means that converge strongly to the origin. A third variant presents Cesàro means whose norms oscillate in the sense that their liminf is zero while their limsup is positive. Thus the strong convergence conclusion in von Neumann's linear mean ergodic theorem does not extend to Baillon's nonlinear mean ergodic theorem, even for firmly nonexpansive mappings.

We provide a variational formulation of a finite-dimensional Follow-the-Leader system through a minimizing-movement scheme based on a discrete transport distance with nonlinear mobility. Despite the degeneracy of the kinetic action at maximal density, we prove finiteness of the distance, $C^1$ regularity of geodesics, and suitable Euler--Lagrange relations. For a decreasing external potential, we show that the JKO scheme yields an approximate implicit Euler discretization of the Follow-the-Leader dynamics. Consequently, as $τ\to0^+$, the piecewise affine interpolations converge, up to a subsequence, to a $C^1$ solution of the continuous Follow-the-Leader system. This complements the many-particle convergence theory for the discrete nonlinear-mobility transport distance by establishing the continuous-time limit at fixed number of particles.

Moreover, smallness in $H^1$ alone is insufficient to close a direct nonlinear elliptic estimate in five dimensions. We overcome these difficulties through uniform Oseen estimates and a relative-energy comparison yielding quadratic improvement of the perturbation. ☆ Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces

This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nyström discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fréchet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. The interface is reconstructed by regularized Gauss--Newton iteration in a Fourier space that is progressively enriched as the frequency increases. Numerical experiments assess direct-solver accuracy and reconstruction performance for different interfaces, material configurations, and noise levels.

☆ On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
Lili Du, Yulan Wang, Yichen Zhang
We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4π$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass \(m<4π\), the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for \(m>4π\), there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. For the fluid-coupled system, Winkler first established global generalized solvability under the condition \(m<2π\) and proposed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2π$ and $4π$. In the present work, we resolve this open problem and show that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact: every admissible initial datum with total mass \(m<4π\) generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded with respect to time. Our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality. The key underlying observation is that combining relative isoperimetric estimates with rearrangement techniques yields a Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality on bounded planar domains with an explicit leading constant.

The total amount of enzyme is fixed, and the substrate concentration is governed by a reaction-diffusion equation with prescribed boundary values. We consider both linear and nonlinear Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics. In previous work, we constructed a maximizing sequence, computed the first and second variations of the reaction functional, and established the nonexistence of local maximizers. Here, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis. We prove that the functional is strictly concave for linear kinetics but need not be concave or convex for nonlinear kinetics. We also show that no critical points exist. We then characterize maximizing sequences and identify all their possible limiting measures. Our analysis reveals the mechanism of reaction maximization through spatial localization: maximizing sequences concentrate enzymes near the portion of the boundary where the substrate concentration is largest. Moreover, the landscape of the functional defining the total reaction differs between the linear and nonlinear cases, a point less emphasized in applications. Consistent with existing biophysical studies, these findings motivate the development and analysis of regularized models.

These periodic solutions form a Delaunay family: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,A)$, there is a unique profile pair, up to translation in $t=\log|x|$, with $\min_{\mathbb{R}}U=\varepsilon$. The Hamiltonian energy provides an alternative parameter, decreasing continuously and strictly from zero to the equilibrium energy as $\varepsilon$ increases from $0$ to $A$. The common least period of the two components tends to infinity as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and to the period of the linearized oscillation at $(A,B)$ as $\varepsilon\uparrow A$. Pierre Monmarché
In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process. The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-Łojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points. In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general Łojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.
♻ ☆ Smooth Piecewise Cutting for Neural Operator to Handle Discontinuities and Sharp Transitions
Ha Dang, Sebastian Schmidt, Juergen Hesser
Neural operators have achieved strong performance in learning solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their inherently continuous representations struggle to capture discontinuities and sharp transitions. Existing approaches typically approximate such features within continuous function spaces, often requiring increased model capacity and high-resolution data. In this work, we propose Cut-DeepONet, a two-stage training framework that explicitly models discontinuities while reducing learning complexity. Our approach reformulates the problem via a lifting strategy, partitioning the domain into smooth subregions while representing discontinuities as boundaries in a higher-dimensional space. This separation aligns the operator learning task with the inductive bias of neural networks and avoids directly approximating discontinuities. An additional network predicts input-dependent discontinuity locations for unseen inputs, which are then used to guide the neural operator in generating smooth components within each region. Experiments on benchmark PDEs show that Cut-DeepONet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, even when trained on low-resolution datasets. The method excels on problems with discontinuities and sharp transitions, while using fewer trainable parameters. Our results highlight the benefits of changing the representation of operator learning rather than increasing model complexity.
