♻ ☆ Regularity for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption
Jiangwen Wang, João Vitor da Silva, Feida Jiang
In this paper, we investigate dead-core problems for fully nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with strong absorption, \begin{equation*} |Du|^{p} F(D^{2}u) - u_{t} = λ_{0}(x,t)\, u^μ\, χ_{\{u>0\}}(x,t) \qquad \text{in } \quad Ω_{T} := Ω\times (0,T), \end{equation*} where $0\le p<\infty$, $0<μ<1$ and $u \geq 0 $ is a bounded viscosity solution satisfying $0\le u_t\le A_0u^μ$ in the viscosity sense for some $0\le A_0<\infty$. We establish a sharp and improved parabolic $C^α$-regularity estimate along the free boundary $\partial \{ u > 0 \}$, where \[ α:= \frac{2+p}{1+p-μ} > 1 + \frac{1}{1+p}. \] Moreover, we establish weak geometric properties of solutions, such as non-degeneracy and uniform positive density. As an application, we obtain a Liouville-type theorem for entire solutions and gradient bounds. Finally, as a byproduct of our approach, we derive a new formulation of the gradient decay property and establish a Harnack-type inequality on time slices. It is worth noting that the results presented here extend those in da Silva {\em et al.}(Pacific J. Math., \textbf{300} (2019), 179--213) and (J. Differential Equations., \textbf{264} (2018), 7270--7293) to the degenerate setting, and can be viewed as a parabolic analogue of da Silva {\em et al.} (Math. Nachr., \textbf{294} (2021), 38--55) and Teixeira (Math. Ann., \textbf{364} (2016), 1121--1134).
comment: We have corrected several errors
♻ ☆ Feynman-Kac Representation and the Asymptotic Speed of the Fisher-KPP Equation with Finite-Activity Jump Noise
Yuhong Li, Hao Wen, Jianhua Huang
We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher--KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump Lévy noise, i.e.\ a compensated Poisson random measure of finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jumps and jumps multiplicatively at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman--Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. The representation converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, allowing a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation, we derive sharp upper and lower bounds for the propagation of the front: for every speed $c>2\sqrt{1+a}$ the solution decays exponentially along the ray $x=ct$, while for every speed $c<2\sqrt{1+a}$ it does not. The two together identify the asymptotic speed in the critical-speed sense: the threshold between exponentially decaying and non-decaying fronts equals $2\sqrt{1+a}$ almost surely, an identity proved without any a priori existence of the limit $R_δ(t)/t$. The complementary bounds $2\sqrt{\underlineγ}\le c\le2\sqrt{\overlineγ}$ also hold, with $\overlineγ,\underlineγ$ explicit in $ε$ and $μ$. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which underlie the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, and numerical simulations illustrate the informativeness of the speed bounds.
comment: 46 pages, 2 figures, 1 table
♻ ☆ Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global Hölder regularity
Reshmi Biswas, Alexander Quaas
Let $ C_ω$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $ω\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_ω$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $β^+>0>β^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $β^\pm$. As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/β^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-Δ_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_ω$ do not exist for $0q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$. The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global Hölder regularity for $(-Δ_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible Hölder exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.
comment: Corrected minor typographical and grammatical errors, and improved the organisation and clarity of the exposition. The main results and mathematical arguments remain unchanged
♻ ☆ Boundary-layer separation beyond the square-root law
Ky Giao Duong, Tej-Eddine Ghoul, Sameer Iyer, Yasunori Maekawa
We construct solutions to the two-dimensional stationary Prandtl system under a constant adverse pressure gradient exhibiting a family of distinct separation laws. More precisely, for every integer $\ell\ge1$, we construct smooth initial data for which separation occurs at a finite location $x=x^\ast$, with \[ \partial_y u(x,0) =\mathbf C_\ell(x^\ast-x)^{\ell/2}\bigl(1+o(1)\bigr), \qquad x\uparrow x^\ast, \] where $\mathbf C_\ell>0$ depends on the initial data. We determine the local asymptotic structure of the solution near separation through matched inner and outer expansions based on linearization around the ground state in von Mises variables. This description addresses Open Problem~5 proposed by Oleinik and Samokhin~\cite{OleinikSamok-book-99}. We prove the nonlinear stability of the square-root separation law ($\ell=1$) under small admissible perturbations of the initial data in a suitable topology.
♻ ☆ On the regularity of entropy solutions to stochastic degenerate parabolic equations
Marko Erceg, Kenneth H. Karlsen, Darko Mitrović
We study the regularity of entropy solutions for quasilinear parabolic equations with anisotropic degeneracy and stochastic forcing. Building on previous works, we establish space-time regularity under a non-degeneracy condition that does not require an assumption on the derivative of the symbol of the corresponding kinetic equation, a restriction imposed in earlier studies. This allows us to obtain regularity results for certain equations not accounted for by prior theory, albeit with reduced regularity exponents. Our approach uses a kinetic formulation with two transport equations, one of second order and one of first order, leveraging a form of "parabolic regularity" inherent in these equations that was not utilized in previous studies.
♻ ☆ Bottom-boundary identification using asymptotic observers in dispersive shallow-water models
Vishal Neeraje, Vishal Vasan
In this paper we consider the problem of identifying the bottom-boundary of an ocean basin, particularly in the coastal region where shallow-water theory applies. Our main contribution is the development of an easy-to-implement observer-based approach of identifying the bottom-boundary profile from measurements of the free-surface. Furthermore, we prove that the true profile can be obtained by minimising the long-time observation-error as computed from the observer equations associated with a class of linear dispersive shallow water-wave models. Numerical simulations indicate the same optimisation problem can recover the true profile for the nonlinear versions of the same dispersive water-wave models.
♻ ☆ Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
Yinghao Gong
We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

♻ ☆ Logarithmic upper bounds and axial front selection for spatially periodic lattice Fisher--KPP equations
Yuanyang Hu, Zhenkun Wang
We study the Cauchy problem $u_t=Δ_{\Z^d}u+F(x,u)$ on $\Z^d$ ($d\geq2$) with a spatially periodic Fisher--KPP reaction $F$ and a nonzero, finitely supported initial datum $u_0:\Z^d\to[0,1]$. We establish a logarithmic upper bound on the front position that holds uniformly in the observation direction, with a logarithmic delay coefficient governed by the outward normal to the asymptotic spreading body. When the linearized growth rate $F_s(x,0)$ is independent of the longitudinal coordinate, we prove the matching axial Bramson correction and show that the solution converges uniformly on fixed-width half-tubes to a critical pulsating front up to a bounded, slowly varying phase shift. For critical pulsating profiles $Φ(s,x)$ satisfying $Φ(s,x)\leq C(1+s)\ee^{-λs}$ for $s\geq0$ and $x\in\Z^d$, where $λ>0$ is the critical spatial decay rate, we derive the precise leading-edge asymptotic expansion and prove uniqueness up to translation. As a consequence, in the axial regime we obtain sharp asymptotics for the arrival times $T_θ(x)=\inf\{t\geq0:u(t,x)\geqθ\}$ ($0<θ<1$), including the asymptotic time lag between distinct level sets at a remote site and the period-to-period passage time along the axis. For general periodic linearized growth rates, we introduce a nonlinear subsolution built from a positive quotient of linear Dirichlet evolutions on a retreating domain and formulate sufficient kernel estimates for a matching directional lower bound.
♻ ☆ Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
Alexey Shevyakov
All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.
♻ ☆ Logarithmically Coupled p-Laplacian Systems: From Discrete Ground States to Rigidity and Critical Continuous Limits
Wenzheng Hu
We introduce a new class of logarithmically coupled \(p\)-Laplacian systems on locally finite graphs and in the critical case \(p=N>4\). The coupling poses two challenges: the energy functional is ill-defined on the natural Sobolev space, and loss of the \(L^\infty\)-embedding prevents standard control of logarithmic terms. To resolve this non-separable logarithmic singularity, we develop an \textbf{exponent calibration technique} that converts logarithmic terms into strictly lower-order power estimates. The technique plays an essential role in two critical steps: the existence proof for the regularised problem and the uniform boundedness of regularised ground states that restores compactness. Thus, we prove solvability of the original ill-posed continuous critical equation. In the discrete setting, we identify five new intrinsic structures, including an exact constrained Hessian factorisation and a scalar rigidity index. We complete a discrete--continuous double loop, providing a unified variational framework for logarithmically coupled systems.
comment: 66 pages
♻ ☆ Exponential Decays of Steklov Eigenfunctions for the Magnetic Laplacian
Zhongwei Shen
Consider the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $Λ_β$ associated with the Schrödinger operator $(D+β\A)^2$ with a magnetic potential in a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$, where $β>1$ is the field strength parameter. Assume that the magnetic field $\B=\nabla \times \A$ is of finite type. We show that if $β>β_0$, the ground state for $Λ_β$ decays exponentially away from a neighborhood of the subset of $\partialΩ$, on which $\B$ vanishes to the maximal order.
comment: 15 pages. Minor revision. Accepted for publication in Proc. Amer. Math. Soc
♻ ☆ Resolvent Estimates for the Stokes Operator in a Three-Dimensional Lipschitz Domain
Zhongwei Shen
By refining the approach developed in \cite{AGH-2015, GS2026a}, we establish resolvent estimates in $L^p_σ(Ω)$ for the Stokes operator in a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$ in $\R^3$ for $(3/2)-\e< p\le \infty$, where $\e>0$ depends on $Ω$. As a consequence, the Stokes operator generates a uniformly bounded analytic semigroup in $L^p_σ(Ω)$. The range for $p$ is sharp. The results are particularly surprising, as it is long believed that the $L^p$ resolvent estimates in three-dimensional Lipschitz domains may fail for large $p$. In the appendices we prove an interpolation theorem between $L^2_σ(Ω)$ and $L^\infty_σ(Ω)$. We also show that for $1< p< \infty$ and a bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω$ in $\R^d, d\ge 2$, the resolvent estimate in $L^p(Ω; \C^d)$ can hold only if the Helmholtz projection is bounded on this space. This explains the counter-example constructed in \cite{Deuring-2001}. Finally, we prove that the resolvent estimate may fail in $L^p_σ(Ω)$ for $1< p< (3/2)$ and $d\ge 3$ as a consequence of failure of the Helmholtz decomposition of $L^p(Ω; \C^d)$.
comment: 30 pages. Appendix C is added. It shows that the range $(3/2)-\e< p\le \infty$ is sharp for $d=3$ and the range $(4/3)-\e< p\le \infty$ is sharp for $d=2$. Comments are welcome
♻ ☆ Convergence of iterated restricted mean values to harmonic functions
Mohammad Javaheri
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain and let $δ$ be a continuous positive function on $Ω$ with $B(x,δ(x))\subseteqΩ$ for every $x\inΩ$. Let $σ(f)(x)$ denote the average of $f$ over the ball $B(x,δ(x))$. Restricted mean value theorems give conditions under which a fixed point of $σ$ must be harmonic. We study the dynamical counterpart of this question: the behavior of the iterates $σ^k(f)$. We show that for \emph{every} bounded domain and every bounded measurable $f$ that is continuous at the points of $\partialΩ$, the iterates $σ^k(f)$ converge locally uniformly in $Ω$ to the Perron--Wiener--Brelot solution of the Dirichlet problem with boundary values $f|_{\partialΩ}$, and that the convergence is uniform on $\overlineΩ$ for all continuous $f$ if and only if $Ω$ is regular for the Dirichlet problem. This contains and extends earlier results for $C^{2,α}$ domains with $C^{2,α}$ data and for strictly convex domains with continuous data. We also give explicit rates of convergence: an algebraic rate $O(1/k)$ on domains with a uniform exterior ball condition and a geometric rate on convex domains, when $δ$ is comparable to the distance to the boundary.
Functional Analysis
☆ On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
Eloi Martinet, Leon Bungert
We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.

☆ The Matrix Kawada--Itô Theorem and Harmonic Rigidity on Locally Compact Groups
Ali Jabbari
A positive $M_n$-valued measure on a locally compact group need not have positive convolution products: matrix multiplication preserves neither self-adjointness nor positivity. We prove that this obstruction disappears completely at an idempotent. If $μ\in M(G,M_n)$ is positive and $μ*μ=μ$, then all its matrix values commute and there is a unique finite decomposition \[ μ=\sum_{j=1}^r m_{K_j}\otimes E_j, \] where the $K_j$ are distinct compact subgroups and the $E_j$ are pairwise orthogonal nonzero projections. The result holds for arbitrary locally compact groups, without countability assumptions or a priori commutativity. The proof combines projection-valued dilations, rigidity of contractive idempotent Fourier coefficients, and faithfulness of the regular representation on finite measures over $G\times G$. For normalized positive matrix convolution semigroups, we further identify the Cesàro harmonic projection with convolution by such an idempotent, even if mass escapes to infinity. Its surviving matrix directions are exactly those uniformly confined to a compact subset of the group, yielding an explicit direct Haar-channel decomposition for all $1
☆ Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman spaces are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map
Samir Panja
In this article, we consider weighted Bergman spaces over open unit disk corresponding to nonnegative integrable radial functions with positive mass arbitrarily close to the unit circle. Then we show that Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the weighted Bergman space are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map. This result generalizes the classical characterization of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space due to Brown and Halmos. Moreover, we prove that there is no compact Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman space.

☆ A Regular First-Order Calculus for the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao Geometry
Enrico Sartor
We introduce a notion of intrinsic differentiability for functionals on the space of finite nonnegative measures equipped with the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) distance, also known as the Hellinger--Kantorovich (HK) distance. The resulting static first-order calculus accounts simultaneously for spatial transport and mass reweighting. We characterize regular barycentric logarithms through optimal semicouplings and measurable selections at the transport threshold, and prove their tangency at arbitrary finite source measures. The defining expansion extends to non-optimal semicouplings, with remainder of smaller order than the square root of their cost. This yields differentiation formulas for simultaneous transport and reweighting and uniqueness of the gradients. We also give a sufficient criterion in terms of regular flat derivatives. We characterize differentiability of one half the squared WFR distance by a common optimal Monge transport--growth representation with no target mass created from the cone vertex. Equivalently, the regular barycentric logarithm is unique and its norm equals the distance; the gradient is minus this logarithm. Finally, we formulate the corresponding calculus on probability measures. On $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, WFR differentiability implies intrinsic Wasserstein differentiability, with the transport component of the WFR gradient coinciding with the Wasserstein gradient. Whenever a flat derivative exists, one quarter of the reaction component agrees almost everywhere with its centered representative. As a byproduct we obtain a Wasserstein differentiability result for the squared $\mathrm{WFR}$ distance.
☆ Fourier Positivity and Sharp Poincaré Inequalities on Graphs
Bang-Xian Han, Yuan-He Wang
We prove sharp dimension-free $L^1$-Poincaré inequalities on Hamming cubes, a sharp quadratic $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on product Poisson spaces, and a sharp pseudo-Poincaré inequality on finite abelian Cayley graphs. These inequalities use a generalization of the Beckmann boundary introduced by Ivanisvili, Xie, and Zhang. In particular, we prove that the optimal dimension-free constant in the classical $L^1$-Poincaré inequality on the Hamming cube is $\sqrt{π/2}$, answering a question of Ivanisvili et al. Semigroup duality and explicit Malliavin weights reduce these estimates to integrals of first absolute moments of centered Bernoulli and Poisson sums. The key ingredient is a Fourier positivity principle, which shows that replacing the coefficients by their absolute values can only increase these integrals. For the underlying Bernoulli functional at subquadratic exponents, we also characterize the maximizers and determine their exact phase transitions.
comment: 27 pages
☆ Isometric Classification of Sobolev Spaces
Samir Hamad
We show that the norm obtained by summing the $L^1$ norms of all weak derivatives through order $k$, including the function itself, determines both $n$ and $k$ on the real Sobolev space $W^{k,1}(\R^n)$. Every surjective linear isometry for this norm is given by a translation, a signed permutation of the coordinates and multiplication by a fixed sign $c\in\{-1,1\}$.
☆ The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet: sharp bounds via entropy numbers in $L_\infty$
Dmitriy Bilyk, Sebastian Neumayer, Tino Ullrich
We settle the uniform small deviation conjecture for the Brownian sheet in every dimension $d\ge2$, namely, that the logarithmic exponent is $2d-1$. Our proof proceeds through sharp entropy and Kolmogorov estimates for the associated anchored mixed Sobolev embedding in the uniform norm. Their connection to small deviations is known from the Kuelbs--Li theorem. To establish the entropy estimates, the key is a probabilistic small ball inequality for smooth tensor product atoms whose exceptional set has Gaussian measure exponentially small in the number of atoms. Its proof combines a count of dyadic rectangles with tools from probability, in particular Ehrhard's Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality. This also yields sharp entropy and Kolmogorov number estimates for embeddings of periodic mixed Sobolev, Besov and Nikol'skii classes with smoothness $r>1/2$ in $L_\infty$. Finally, we extend our results to fractional and integrated Brownian sheets.
☆ Ahlfors $1$-Regularity and Conformal Criteria for Carleson Measures
Yihao Hou, Huaying Wei
We prove that a bounded Jordan domain $Ω$ has Ahlfors $1$-regular boundary if and only if the following criterion holds for every positive Borel measure $μ$ on $Ω$: $μ$ is Carleson exactly when $\int_Ω|φ'(w)|\,dμ(w)<\infty$ for every conformal bijection $φ$ from $Ω$ onto a bounded domain with rectifiable boundary. The same characterization holds using only arclength measures on simple locally rectifiable curves, with the integral condition replaced by finite length of every such conformal image. These results extend Bishop's theorem on the unit disk. We also study analogous criteria for vanishing Carleson measures.
☆ Step-isometries on Banach spaces
Ruidong Wang, Li Tang, Jianglong Luo
Step-isometries are maps preserving the integer part of pairwise distances on metric spaces. They arise naturally in the study of infinite random geometric graphs, where graph isomorphisms between LARG-type random graphs reduce to step-isometries on the underlying vertex sets. Several fundamental open problems concerning the rigidity, extendability, and continuity of step-isometries were raised in recent literature, notably by Šemrl, and by Balogh, Walters, and Zsák. In the present paper we resolve a number of these long-standing open questions. We establish rigidity results for step-isometries defined on norm-dense subsets of both real and complex Banach spaces. For complex Banach spaces, we prove that every almost-surjective step-isometry on a norm-dense subset admits a unique extension to a surjective real-affine isometry of the whole space. In the real setting, we investigate three key properties $A$, $B$, $C$ formulated by Šemrl, which ask whether certain classes of step-isometries extend to surjective affine isometries. We verify these properties for uniformly non-square Banach spaces, for spaces with a dense set of Fréchet-smooth points, and for strictly convex Banach spaces with separable dual. In particular, we confirm Conjecture 2 due to Balogh, Walters, and Zsák without countability assumptions on the dense domain set. We further show that every bijective step-isometry defined on the entire Banach space is a homeomorphism, answering their Question 3 affirmatively. Specializing to $\ell_1^n$, we obtain that $\ell_1^n$ satisfies Property $A$ for all integers $n\ge 3$, settling an open problem posed by Šemrl.
☆ Trace and Regularized Index of Callias Operators on Hyperbolic Space
Jilly Kevo
Let $d \geq 3$ be odd. On hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$, we consider Callias-type operators, i.e. Dirac-Schrödinger operators of the form $D = ic \nabla + A$, where $c \nabla$ is the Dirac operator and $A$ a function with values in the self-adjoint operators, and provide an explicit formula for the iterated trace $\text{tr}_{L^2(\mathbb{H}^d,H)} \text{tr}_{S}( e^{-tD^*D} - e^{-tDD^*})$, $t>0$, that appears in the formulation of the Witten index. Thereby, the operator $D$ is not assumed to be Fredholm.
comment: 66 pages
☆ Isomorphisms and representations of noncommutative function algebras
Marcel Scherer, Orr Shalit, Eli Shamovich, Mansi Suryawanshi
Let $V$ be a noncommutative (NC) variety in a NC operator ball. We study the dual operator algebra $H^\infty(V)$ of bounded NC functions on $V$, and the operator algebra $A(V)$ obtained as the closure of NC polynomials in $H^\infty(V)$. We identify the space of weak-$*$ continuous finite-dimensional representations of $H^\infty(V)$ as the similarity envelope $\widetilde{V}$ of $V$, and equip $\widetilde{V}$ with a metric which turns $\widetilde{V}$ into a complete invariant for $H^\infty(V)$, in the sense that $H^\infty(V)$ is weak-$*$ continuously isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if $\widetilde{V}$ and $\widetilde{W}$ are NC biholomorphic via a bi-Lipschitz map. Similar results are obtained in the completely bounded category as well as for the algebras $A(V)$ when $V$ is assumed homogeneous. In the case of homogeneous varieties $V$ and $W$, we obtain a sharper classification result, by which $H^\infty(V)$ is (completely) boundedly isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if there is a linear map which gives a bi-Lipschitz bijection between $\widetilde{W}$ and $\widetilde{V}$. The reduction to the linear case in the generality we work in depends on showing that the existence of maps implies the existence of origin-fixing maps, which we show using a novel ``two-circle trick" of independent interest. In the important case where the varieties are the full NC operator balls we find a striking rigidity phenomenon: if $A(B_E)$ and $A(B_F)$ are completely boundedly isomorphic then $E$ and $F$ are completely isometric. We also present a variety of examples illustrating the results and their sharpness, showing how several results from the literature fail to generalize to the setting studied here.

☆ Commuting Toeplitz and Little Hankel Operators on the Bidisk
Lei Chen
Necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained for two Toeplitz operators and for a Toeplitz operator and a little Hankel operator to commute on the pluriharmonic Hardy space of the bidisk.
☆ A Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull characterization of inner-product spaces via Birkhoff--James orthogonality
Zhiyao Fang, Junxiang Qi, Qi Liu
The classical location problem posed by Weber [Über den Standort der Industrien,Tübingen: J. C. B. Mohr, 1909] has motivated various geometric characterizations of inner-product spaces. Benítez, Fernández and Soriano [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. \textbf{354} (2002), 5027--5038] characterized real inner-product spaces through the convex-hull property of Fermat--Torricelli medians.Pakhrou [J. Funct. Anal. \textbf{285} (2023), 110078] further established a characterization using $γ$-centers and equilateral triangles. Building on these results, we show that the Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull criterion remains valid when restricted to triples satisfying a one-sided Birkhoff--James orthogonality condition.The proof combines norming functionals, radial rescaling,Alexandrov differentiability, and the area formula.No completeness, smoothness, or strict convexity assumptions are required.
☆ Entropy and frame measures for self-similar measures
Zhiyong Wang, Wei Tang
For $0<ρ<1$ and a set of $N\ge2$ distinct real digits $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\mathbb{R}$, let \[ μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}=\frac1N\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}\circ S_i^{-1}, \qquad S_i(x)=ρ(x+d_i). \] Write $X=\sum_{j\ge1}ρ^j d_{ω_j}$, where the symbols $ω_j$ are independent and uniform on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$. We prove that $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy $H(ω_1\mid X)>0$. In particular, this holds for all $ρ>1/N$, without any absolute-continuity assumption or arithmetic restriction on the digits or the contraction. At $ρ=1/N$, for commensurable digits, a frame measure exists if and only if $μ_{ρ,\mathscr D}$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor. For $\mathscr D=\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ and $ρ<1/N$, we also prove nonexistence whenever $ρ^{-m}=a/b$ for some $m\in\N$, with $a/b$ in lowest terms, $b\mid N$ and $N/b\nmid a$, extending the integer-power obstruction. The extension compares mask quotients using finite families of target pole classes in place of one target class.
☆ Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
María J. Beltrán-Meneu, Jorga Galindo, Enrique Jordá
We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(Δ(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $Δ(\mathfrak{A})$ is $σ$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.
☆ A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
Bowoo Kang, Jaechul Lee, Zhenghao Li
On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(θ,μ)$, where $μ$ is a positive Radon measure and $$θ=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $μ$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators. Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $μ$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.

☆ Characterization of Attenuated V-Line Transform and Direct Reconstruction from Samples
Youfa Li, Lvchang Li
The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ($L^2$-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $s>2$.
☆ Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications
Sergo A. Episkoposian
Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.

☆ Finite-rank Toeplitz commutators on the harmonic Bergman space
Puyu Cui, Zengyong Huang, Yufeng Lu, Chao Zu
We completely characterize finite-rank commutators of Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk. Apart from affine dependence, finite rank occurs precisely when both symbols are analytic with rational primitives, or both are coanalytic and their complex conjugates have rational primitives. Our approach combines a block-matrix decomposition with Luecking's theorem, which rules out nonzero finite-rank Toeplitz operators with bounded symbols on the Bergman space. In particular, every such finite-rank commutator has square zero.

☆ Power Mean, Karcher Mean, and Log-Euclidean Mean on Positive Constant Upper Triangular Matrices
Huajun Huang, Sejong Kim, Vatsalkumar N. Mer
We study weighted power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means on the Lie group CP_n of real upper triangular matrices with a constant positive diagonal. Building on the general triangular-group theory, we use the central decomposition CP_n \cong \mathbb R_+ -by-UP_n to separate the scalar power mean from a unipotent mean with reweighted coefficients. We prove that the power mean extends real-analytically through order zero, where it equals the Karcher mean. We establish exterior-power covariance for the Karcher and log-Euclidean means, and tensor-product identities for all three means, distinguishing product weights from paired inputs. Finite nilpotent functional calculus yields concise formulas on CP_2 and CP_3, where the Karcher and log-Euclidean means coincide. In dimension four, their difference is exactly a central cubic commutator, giving a necessary and sufficient equality criterion and an explicit counterexample. In every dimension, the same commutator is the leading term of their small-dispersion difference.
☆ Disjointness preserving operators on Köthe-Banach spaces
Iryna Krasikova, Mikhail Popov, Beata Randrianantoanina
A well-known result of Abramovich says that if $E$, $F$ are rearrangement invariant Banach spaces on a finite atomless measure space such that $E$ has an absolutely continuous norm and $E\not\subseteq F$, then there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$. We obtain an analogue of this result in the setting of general Köthe-Banach spaces. Specifically, we identify a sufficient condition on Köthe-Banach spaces $E$, $F$ on finite atomless measure spaces that implies that there are no nonzero disjointness preserving bounded linear operators $T \colon E\to F$. Consequently, by a representation theorem for regular operators due to O.~Maslyuchenko, Mykhaylyuk and the second named author, this condition implies that every regular linear operator $T \colon E\to F$ is narrow. As an application, we obtain that if $1\le \max\{p_1,p_2\}< \min\{ r_1, r_2\}\le \infty$, then every regular linear operator $T \colon L_{p_1}(L_{p_2}) \to L_{r_1}(L_{r_2})$ is narrow. The latter may be seen as an analogue of the classical Pitt compactness theorem.
☆ Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
Zengjian Lou, Jinbang Wen
We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

☆ A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic
José Iovino
The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations, and Reggio proved the theorem equivalent to the Beth definability property of an infinitary equational logic. We extend both results beyond compactness: on every separable metric space, and in particular on every Polish space, every bounded uniformly continuous function is a uniform limit of functions built from countably many bounded separating functions by the connectives of infinitary real-valued logic, and an approximate Beth property of this logic is equivalent to the new theorem. The extension rests on a rule of syntax, which admits a countable supremum when its terms share an a priori bound and thereby makes the sentences define exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and on a model existence game that does the work of compactness in the proof of interpolation.
☆ Empirical approximation of $L_p$ norms for $p\in (2, \infty)$
Feng Dai, Egor Kosov, Noel Murasko
For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(μ)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(μ)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $ξ^1,\ldots,ξ^m$ with distribution $μ$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(ξ^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(μ)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.

☆ Characterizations of minimal Hermitian completions via moments and subdifferentials
Tamara Bottazzi, Alejandro Varela
Given a Hermitian matrix $A_0$ and a real subspace $W$ of Hermitian matrices, we study the matrices $A_0+W_0$, $W_0\in W$, of minimal spectral norm, which we call $W$-minimal. The main motivation is the Hermitian matrix completion problem, where $W$ is spanned by the Hermitian matrix units corresponding to the unspecified entries. Our main tool is the moment of a subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ relative to $W$, a compact convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^r$, $r=\dim(W)$, which we relate to the joint numerical range and to the $k$-dimensional field of a family of matrices. We compute the subdifferential of $\|A_0+W(x)\|$ in terms of the moments of the eigenspaces of the extreme eigenvalues of $A_0+W(x)$, and we obtain several equivalent characterizations of $W$-minimality: in terms of eigenvectors, of moments, of subdifferentials and of norm one functionals that annihilate $W$. When the identity belongs to $W$, every $W$-minimal matrix has balanced spectrum, and minimality is equivalent to the moments of the eigenspaces of the maximum and minimum eigenvalues having nonempty intersection; we show that this characterization fails if $I\notin W$. We illustrate the results with several examples, and we prove that the adjacency matrix of a connected graph is minimal for its completion problem if and only if the graph is complete bipartite.

☆ A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
Yoonje Jeong, Sang-Gyun Youn
For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|χ_u+χ_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.
♻ ☆ Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
Gerardo Barrera, Jonas M. Tölle
We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-δ})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $δ>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.

♻ ☆ Coarse comparison of Bessel families
Nizar El Idrissi
A Bessel family is a collection of vectors of a Hilbert space whose coefficients are square summable; orthonormal bases and frames are examples. We compare two such families by asking when the size of the coefficients of one is controlled, up to constants, by that of the other after a change of variables taken from a fixed class $\mathcal O$ of operators. Each class (bounded, injective, bounded below, invertible, Fredholm, and others) gives an equivalence relation that ignores redundancy and treats frames and nonframes on the same footing. For every relation we determine the classes by explicit spectral data: the singular numbers of the analysis operator, its kernel, the closedness of its range, and the multiplicities of its spectrum at each dyadic scale. We also characterize the families equivalent to an orthonormal basis, compute an operator Banach--Mazur distance, and prove a Paley--Wiener stability result that needs no frame assumption. These relations are instances of the comparison categories of a companion article.

♻ ☆ Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity
Ma Yicen
We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors with alternating small differences lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for norm-sigma-compact DSS families and uniform nuclear tails on each compact piece. For norm-compact families we also obtain common Hilbert-space factors and uniformly small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. We present the main argument as a candidate proof over the real field.
♻ ☆ The maximal monotonicity of the subdifferential in locally convex spaces via upper envelopes
M. D. Voisei
We establish equivalent conditions for the convex subdifferential to be maximal monotone in general settings, expressed in terms of the associated upper envelopes.
♻ ☆ Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
Leon Bungert, Lucas Schmitt
Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

♻ ☆ A family of matrix flows converging to normal matrices
Masaki Izumi
The celebrated Antezana-Pujals-Stojanoff Theorem states that the iterated Aluthge transforms of an arbitrary matrix converge to a normal matrix. We introduce a family of matrix flows that share this convergence property by defining them through ordinary differential equations. The family includes a continuous analogue of the Aluthge transform, as well as a differential equation discussed by Haagerup in the context of II$_1$ factors. We also examine the same type of flows in the setting of Hilbert space operators equipped with unitarily invariant norms.

♻ ☆ Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
Mingming Cao
We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The main result states that, under the assumption of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Based on this result, we also establish multilinear extrapolation of boundedness on rearrangement invariant Banach function spaces, and multilinear extrapolation of compactness on general Banach function spaces. Beyond that, we give characterizations of the boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on both general Banach function spaces and certain specific function spaces. All results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.

We study open-mapping, continuous-inverse and closed-graph properties for maps whose domain and range belong to the same class of Hausdorff topological vector spaces. ♻ ☆ Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
Yinghao Gong
We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

♻ ☆ A Novel Two-Parameter Penalty: Relaxation Degree Analysis and Sparse Signal Recovery
Ziwei Li, Wengu Chen, Huanmin Ge, Dachun Yang
In this article, we introduce a nonconvex two-parameter penalty function $P_{a,p}$, parameterized by $a\in(0,\infty)$ and $p\in(0,1]$, and the relaxation degree RD$_P$ for a separable nonconvex penalty function $P$. Based on $P_{a,p}$, we further propose the $P_{a,p}$ minimization framework for sparse signal recovery. This framework generalizes the TL1 minimization model established by S. Zhang and J. Xin (corresponding to the special case $p=1$) and provides a unified family of nonconvex penalty functions for sparse signal recovery. Using the sparse convex-combination technique, we establish both exact and stable sparse signal recovery under the restricted isometry property (RIP). To efficiently solve the resulting nonconvex optimization problem, we apply a modified iteratively re-weighted least squares method and the difference of convex functions algorithm (DCA) to develop the IRLSTLp algorithm for unconstrained $P_{a,p}$ minimization and prove some convergence results. Finally, numerical experiments compare recovery and runtime against single- and double-loop baselines, examine sensitivity to $(a,p)$, and assess the empirical correlation between RD$_{P_{a,p}}$ and recovery within the proposed family.
♻ ☆ A Time-Frequency Framework for GKP Codes
Franz Luef, Eduard Ortega
We develop a time--frequency framework for lattice GKP codes in which ideal codewords are realized in the modulation space $M^\infty$ and identified, through a vector-valued Zak transform, with a finite logical fibre over the continuous syndrome torus. Multi-window Gabor analysis then represents the logical vector by a finite block of adjoint-lattice coefficients. We prove that the normalized block map is an isometry, obtain an explicit recovering projection, and derive stable logical reconstruction. We further construct normalizable GKP approximants as lattice-envelope Gabor multipliers and establish weak-$*$ convergence and asymptotically isometric encoding. Finally, we recover displacement syndromes from phase relations between translated coefficient blocks and quantify their stability under additive perturbations.

♻ ☆ Multipoint Characterization of Higher-Order Sobolev Spaces
Kacper Kurowski
In the paper, we prove a rather general characterization of higher-order Sobolev spaces. We show that the $k\mathrm{th}$-order regularity, where $k \in \mathbb{N}$, is captured via inequalities involving $2^k$-tuples of points. In fact, in full generality, the obtained results characterize higher-order Sobolev spaces based on Banach function spaces. Moreover, we show an analogous characterization of higher-order Hölder spaces. Finally, we propose a way to use the obtained results to define higher-order Sobolev and Hölder spaces on metric measure spaces.
♻ ☆ Compact Quasi-Metric Spaces Are Expand-Contract Plastic
Thomas Duzer
On a totally bounded metric space, every non-contractive self-map is an isometry. For quasi-metric spaces this fails. Here quasi-metrics are $T_1$: $d(x,y)=0$ implies $x=y$. Zavarzina gave a hereditarily precompact counterexample and asked whether rigidity holds at least for bijections. The author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) shows that it does not. We prove that compactness restores it: every compact quasi-metric space is expand-contract plastic, that is, each of its bijective non-contractive self-maps is an isometry. Countable compactness suffices, as does compactness of the conjugate topology. Bijectivity is needed, even on a compact, hereditarily precompact space. For arbitrary non-contractive self-maps, we prove rigidity when the space is hereditarily precompact and its conjugate topology is sequentially compact, in particular when it is also Yoneda complete; neither hypothesis can be dropped. Such maps are then surjective. In both theorems the $T_1$ axiom can be weakened to $R_0$, $d(x,y)=0$ implies $d(y,x)=0$, if hereditary precompactness is taken to mean that every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; surjectivity then holds up to points at distance 0 both ways. The weaker $T_0$ axiom is not enough: there is a $T_0$ space, compact in both topologies and satisfying all the other hypotheses of both theorems, with a bijective non-contractive non-isometry. Finally, for an asymmetric norm in finite dimension, the classical theorem makes the symmetric unit ball and sphere rigid for all non-contractive self-maps, and the forward ones if the norm is $T_1$. In infinite dimension, the symmetric ball and sphere need not be plastic, and for the forward ones we pose the quasi-metric form of the unit-ball question of Cascales, Kadets, Orihuela and Wingler. The two theorems and the counterexamples of Section 6 are machine-checked in Lean, except the steps listed at the end.

♻ ☆ Bijective Non-Contractive Maps of Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Spaces Need Not Be Isometries
Thomas Duzer
Zavarzina asked whether every bijective non-contractive self-map of a precompact quasi-metric space is an isometry. We show that it need not be, even when the space is hereditarily precompact. On the integers, take the distance of an irrational rotation and add a fixed toll $c>0$ to every step from a nonnegative integer down to a smaller one. The resulting space, the toll spiral, is a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, and the shift $n\mapsto n+1$ is a bijective non-contractive map that is not an isometry. The construction works over any metric space $Y$: for every bijective isometry $σ$ of $Y$ and every point whose $σ$-orbit is aperiodic and totally bounded, adding the same toll along the orbit gives such a counterexample, for instance over the $p$-adic odometer. The conjugate of the toll spiral is not even precompact, so the hypothesis on the conjugate in Zavarzina's positive result cannot be dropped, even for bijections. The toll spiral is also not expand-contract plastic, since the inverse shift is a non-expansive bijection that is not an isometry. For an arbitrary bijective non-contractive map $F$, the distance from $F^kx$ to $F^ky$ has a limit as $k\to-\infty$; $F$ is an isometry for this limit, and the excess $D_0$ of the distance over it is the defect. On a hereditarily precompact space, we prove a monochromy theorem: if a pair $(a,b)$ has positive defect $η$, then there are natural numbers $t_1η/4$ for every difference $Δ=t_j-t_i$ with $iη/4$ for every such $Δ$. Three boundary results delimit the remaining question; the open case, that of separated spaces compact in one of their topologies, has since been settled by the author (arXiv:2610.14301). The construction, in general and for the circle, is machine-checked in Lean 4 using Mathlib, with no unproved steps.

☆ On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
Gongping Niu
In this paper, we prove that every complete noncompact two-sided properly embedded constant mean curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal. The result holds in every dimension. We assume no bounds on curvature or volume growth. This establishes the properly embedded case of the finite-index version of do Carmo's question. For nonzero mean curvature, we use the radii of inscribed balls to define a positive weight. This weight gives a polynomial bound on weighted volume, while its reciprocal satisfies a differential inequality involving the Jacobi operator. We combine these properties with stability outside a compact set to obtain finite total area. This leads to a contradiction.

☆ The isoperimetric problem in the Riemannian Heisenberg $3$-space
José M. Espinar, Pablo Mira
We prove that every closed weakly stable constant mean curvature surface immersed in the Riemannian Heisenberg space ${\rm Nil}_3$ is an embedded rotational sphere. As a consequence, we solve the isoperimetric problem in ${\rm Nil}_3$: the isoperimetric domains of ${\rm Nil}_3$ are exactly the regions enclosed by rotational constant mean curvature spheres, and for each prescribed volume there is a unique such domain, up to ambient isometry. For small volumes, the isoperimetric result was proved by Tomter in 1993.

☆ Gradient higher integrability for a general class of degenerate parabolic double phase systems
Bogi Kim, Jehan Oh, Abhrojyoti Sen
We establish quantitative local higher integrability estimates for weak solutions of degenerate parabolic systems with generalized double phase growth, whose prototype is $$u_t-\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{G'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du+a(x,t)\frac{H'(|Du|)}{|Du|}Du\right)=0\qquad\text{in }Ω_T.$$ Here $G$ and $H$ are Young functions satisfying suitable structural assumptions. The nonnegative coefficient $a$ is allowed to vanish and has a concave modulus of continuity $ω$ with respect to the parabolic distance. For $Ψ(z,\varkappa)=G(\varkappa)+a(z)H(\varkappa)$, we prove that solutions in $L^\infty(0,T;L^s(Ω,\mathbb{R}^N))$, $2\le s<\infty$, satisfy $Ψ(\cdot,|Du|)\in L^{1+\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, provided $$\limsup_{ρ\to 0+}ω(ρ)\frac{H(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}{G(ρ^{-\frac{n+s}{s}})}<\infty.$$ For bounded solutions, the corresponding condition involves $H(ρ^{-1})/G(ρ^{-1})$. These conditions extend the known interpolative gap bounds from power growth to general growth functions and continuity moduli. In particular, for $G(\varkappa)=\varkappa^p$, $H(\varkappa)=\varkappa^q$, and $ω(ρ)\simeqρ^α$, they recover $q\le p+sα/(n+s)$ and $q\le p+α$, respectively. The proof combines an intrinsic stopping-time argument with inverse-function estimates to derive Poincaré and reverse Hölder inequalities adapted to the general growth phases.

☆ Shock solutions of a 3D spherical piston problem for the compressible Euler equations
Pengfei Zhou, Huimin Yu, Xiaomin Zhang
This paper establishes the global well-posedness of shock solutions for a 3D spherical piston problem to the compressible Euler equations. The main mathematical challenges are the nonlinear coupling between the free shock boundary and the moving piston, alongside potential gradient catastrophes induced by spherical geometric source terms. To overcome these difficulties, we reformulate the problem using Riemann invariants and introduce a tailored directional derivative along the unperturbed piston trajectory. Then we can extend the local solution to construct a global piecewise smooth solution including a single shock under some moderate assumptions.
☆ Uniqueness of Extremizers and Convergence of the Euler-Lagrange Iteration for the Critical Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev Inequality

For diagonal dilatation with $-2<γ\leq0$ and cylindrical dilatation with $-3/2<γ\leq0$, with or without shear, we construct global homogeneous solutions for small data and prove their stability under small spatially inhomogeneous perturbations. In scaled variables, the perturbations remain uniformly controlled in deformation-adapted spaces and decay in mixed spatial--velocity norms, algebraically in the diagonal regime and exponentially in the cylindrical regime. For homogeneous simple shear with $-2\leqγ\leq0$, we prove global existence and uniqueness for nonnegative data with finite mass and Fisher information, without smallness or a finite-energy assumption. These solutions conserve mass and propagate additional Sobolev regularity. For spatially inhomogeneous simple shear with $-2<γ\leq0$, we establish global well-posedness for small data. The analysis combines commuting vector fields, dispersive and bilinear collision estimates, and integrability of the rescaled collision coefficients. For homogeneous shear, a positivity-preserving splitting transfers Fisher-information control to rough data, while a Lorentz-space estimate includes the endpoint $γ=-2$ in the global continuation argument.
☆ Well-posedness and large deviations for 3D primitive equations with jumps
Zhuoyang Shen, Xinhua Li, Chunyou Sun
We establish the global pathwise well-posedness and a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for the three-dimensional viscous primitive equations driven by multiplicative Lévy noise represented by a compensated Poisson random measure. Under local Lipschitz and moment growth assumptions on the noise coefficient, we construct local martingale solutions and obtain a unique maximal pathwise solution with càdlàg trajectories in the $H^1$ energy space. Additional sixth-moment growth in $H^1$ and $L^6$ growth bounds on the baroclinic component of the noise yield global pathwise well-posedness. The proof combines the jump Itô formula with baroclinic and anisotropic energy estimates to rule out finite-time blow-up. Under further exponential integrability and structural assumptions on the noise coefficient, we establish a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle in a strong path topology by the weak convergence approach.

☆ Global regularity of the two-dimensional fractional Boussinesq equations with critical dissipation
Qian Li, Jiahong Wu, Xiaojing Xu, Zhuan Ye
In the present paper, our primary focus is on the Boussinesq equations with fractional velocity dissipation $Λ^αu$ and temperature diffusion $Λ^βθ$. On the critical balance line $α+β=1$, establishing global regularity for weak velocity dissipation has been obstructed by the quadratic convective-buoyancy feedback, and all available results below $α=\frac{10}{13}$ require a smallness assumption on the initial temperature. In this paper, we prove large-data global regularity across the extended regime $α>\frac{\sqrt{57}-5}{4} \approx 0.637$. This provides a step beyond the previous barrier $α=\frac{10}{13}$, unconditionally dismantling the temperature smallness assumption that has persisted in the literature for over a decade. The mathematical mechanism relies on a high-order Quadratic Normal Form transformation $H=ω-R_αθ-\Bop(θ,θ)$ tailored to eliminate non-resonant quadratic vorticity-temperature interactions. Crucially, by uncovering the exact physical scalings of the underlying multilinear commutators and maintaining sharp fractional conjugates in the $L^m$-energy framework, we ensure that the global energy closure is governed entirely by the quadratic thermal dissipation. Once an integrability threshold $m>\frac{2}α$ is attained, a fine Littlewood-Paley transport estimate drives a fractional regularity gain $H \in B_{r,\infty}^{3α-2}$, ensuring the velocity field achieves critical drift regularity $C^α$. By Silvestre-type drift regularization, this spontaneously generates positive Hölder continuity for the temperature, which in turn elevates the drift regularity strictly beyond the critical threshold, unlocking non-local Schauder estimates to prevent finite-time singularity formation.

☆ A new characterization of the round sphere

We provide an elementary proof of Hersch's inequality and Cheng's theorem, both characterizing the sphere. We revisit these classical results in connection with the geodesic monotonicity of heat kernels on two-dimensional spheres, which provides a third characterization.

☆ Regularity of Weak Solutions near Singular Minimizing Cones for the One-Phase Free Boundary Problem
Minyoung Jeong
Alt and Caffarelli proved an Allard-type $ε$-regularity theorem near the flat one-homogeneous minimizer of the one-phase free boundary problem. A natural follow-up question is whether an analogous regularity result holds near singular minimizing cones. In this paper, we prove such an $ε$-regularity theorem near a strongly integrable one-phase minimizing cone with an isolated singularity. More precisely, we show that, after a suitable translation and rotation, the free boundary of any non-degenerate weak solution sufficiently close to the cone is graphical over the free boundary of a leaf of the De Silva--Jerison--Shahgholian foliation. This result is analogous to recent $ε$-regularity theorems in minimal surface theory by Edelen and by Edelen--Spolaor; our proof adapts the strategy of Edelen to the one-phase setting.
☆ Non-conical classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated singularity
Minyoung Jeong
Several examples of one-homogeneous classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated free boundary singularity are known. Adapting the approach of Caffarelli, Hardt, and Simon for minimal surfaces, we construct non-conical classical solutions with an isolated free boundary singularity by perturbing a one-homogeneous solution $U$. Moreover, if $U$ is strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate), then any solution sufficiently close to $U$ is also strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate).
☆ Blow-Up and Life-Span for Nonlinear Hardy-Hénon Parabolic Equations
Byrame Ben Slimene, Slim Tayachi
We consider the nonlinear Hardy-Hénon parabolic equation $ u_t=Δu+|x|^l|u|^αu,$ $t>0,$ $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$ or $x\in\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}$, with $N\ge1$, $l>-\min\{2,N\}$, $α>0$, with nonnegative initial datum $u_0$. We first establish new criteria for finite-time blow-up. We then derive optimal upper bounds for the life-span $T_{\max}(λ\varphi)$ of solutions arising from the initial datum $u_0=λ\varphi$. These estimates establish a precise dependence of $T_{\max}(λ\varphi)$ on both the initial profile $\varphi$ and the parameter $λ$ in the small and large-amplitude regimes.
☆ Regularity of elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure
Jihoon Ok
We study autonomous elliptic systems with Uhlenbeck structure of the form \[ -\operatorname{div}\big(\mathfrak a(|Du|)Du\big)=0 \quad \text{in }\ Ω\subset \mathbb R^n \] Under two-sided quantitative $(p,q)$-growth conditions on $\mathfrak a$, we prove gradient Hölder continuity with constants and exponent depending only on the dimensions, $p$ and $q$. This improves the classical theory initiated by Uhlenbeck by removing the continuity requirement on $\mathfrak a'$. The proof uses nonlinear comparison systems whose regularity follows from a scalar uniformly elliptic equation. Under weaker $(p,q)$-growth conditions on the convex function $\varphi(t):=\int_0^t s\mathfrak a(s)\,ds$, we obtain local $W^{1,s}$-regularity for every $s>1$, and hence Hölder continuity of solutions with every exponent less than one. An additional lower growth condition on $\mathfrak a$ yields local Lipschitz continuity, even when $\mathfrak a$ is discontinuous.

The following equation is considered: $$-Δ_p u(\boldsymbol{x}) + Δ_q u(\boldsymbol{x}) = f\big(\boldsymbol{x}, u(\boldsymbol{x})\big)\text{ for } \boldsymbol{x} \in Ω, \qquad u(\boldsymbol{x}) = 0 \text{ for } \boldsymbol{x}\in \partial Ω.$$ We start by showing that the energy functional associated with the considered problem no longer has the properties typical of its non-competing counterpart, which prevents a direct application of standard variational and monotonicity methods. Using Ekeland's variational principle combined with properties imposed on the nonlinear term~$f$, we prove the existence of a nonzero generalized solution to the problem. It is also shown that in the one-dimensional case $Ω= (-1,1)$, assuming that $f$ satisfies the symmetry conditions $$f(x,u) = f(-x,u) = -f(x,-u),$$ together with the sign condition $f(x,u) \geq 0$ for $u \geq 0$ and an appropriate growth bound on $f$, a convex relaxation of the action functional yields the existence of a positive weak solution. Furthermore, we prove that in this setting, and under a slightly stronger sign condition $$f(x,u) > 0\text{ for }u > 0,$$ all global minimizers of the action functional do not vanish in $(-1,1)$ but fail to be of class $C^1$.

We study, at the logarithmic mollification scale $η^{-2(d+1+α)}\leδ\log N$ of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, the fluctuation field $V^N=\sqrt N(μ^N-u_η)$ of the moderately interacting multi-species particle system whose mean-field limit is the Shigesada- Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system. The field is centred at the solution $u_η$ of the mollified equation, which depends on $N$ through $η$. On a scale of weighted Bessel-potential spaces of negative order we prove that the laws of $(V^N,M^N)$ are tight, where $M^N$ is the martingale part. Every limit point of $M^N$ is a continuous Gaussian martingale with an explicit deterministic bracket. Every limit point of $V^N$ is a weak solution, and the mild solution, of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SPDE whose drift is the linearisation of the SKT operator at the limit $u$. The initial field and the martingale are independent, and weak solutions are unique given both, so the whole sequence converges in law, jointly with the martingale part, and the limit is unique in law among solutions of the martingale problem. The noise is $d M_i=div(\sqrt{2u_iΘ_i}dW_i)$, with $Θ_i=σ_i+\sum_jf(a_{ij}u_j)$ and $W$ a cylindrical Wiener process on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^{nd})$. The hypotheses are those of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{ü}ngel, including the smallness and the nonnegativity on $\mathbb{R}$ of the nonlinearity $f$. We add radial kernels $B_{ij}$, the independence of the initial data and the Brownian motions across particles and species, a smaller $δ$, a regularity budget on $u_0$, a strengthened smallness condition on $f$ that makes the backward system diagonally dominant in weighted spaces, and an integer Sobolev index $s$.
♻ ☆ Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
Hoan Nguyen
We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. Moreover, the perturbed foliation admits a common smooth calibration, hence the lifted leaves are area-minimizing. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

♻ ☆ On statistical inference for non-linear dynamical systems evolving in their global attractor
Dimitri Konen, Richard Nickl
We consider a periodic scalar reaction-diffusion system over a two-dimensional domain under natural conditions on the reaction function and with initial condition $θ$. We show that on the global attractor $\mathcal A$ of the resulting dynamical system $(u_θ(t):t>0)$, a reverse Poincaré inequality holds true, and that as a consequence the map $θ\mapsto u_θ(t)$ satisfies an $L^2(\Om)$-Lipschitz stability estimate on $\mathcal A$ for any $t>0$ fixed. We then show that statistical recovery of an initial condition $θ$ in the attractor $\mathcal A$, as well as prediction of the states $u_θ$, is possible from discrete measurements of the system at parametric $1/\sqrt N$ convergence rates.
♻ ☆ Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
Khalil Chouk, Massimiliano Gubinelli, Guopeng Li, Jiawei Li, Tadahiro Oh
(Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.

♻ ☆ The kinetic Kato square root problem
Kaj Nyström
We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.

♻ ☆ Non-simple blow-up for the Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on Riemannian surfaces
Youngae Lee, Lei Zhang
The existence and structure of non-simple blow-up are fundamental questions for the self-dual Chern--Simons--Higgs equation. Physically, this phenomenon describes magnetic-flux concentration in several cores whose mutual distances are much larger than their widths, although all cores approach the same vortex point. Despite substantial progress for singular Liouville equations, the existence of non-simple blow-up solutions to the full Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on closed surfaces has remained open in both the Chern--Simons (CS) and mean-field regimes. We prove that the cores of every non-simple cluster have equal limiting masses, share a common profile type, and form an asymptotically regular polygon. These identities yield an explicit finite list of admissible cluster masses and a four-unit mass-gap criterion. We also construct non-simple blow-up solutions on closed Riemannian surfaces in both regimes. Together, these results establish a sharp arithmetic criterion for single-point non-simple CS blow-up on each fixed flat torus when a suitable exterior divisor may be chosen, and show that vortex blow-up need not be simple, answering Li--Liu's question in the negative.
